material.explanation: Creates a Blender material whose Principled BSDF shader inputs are set from the options: colour drives Base Color and Alpha, and the other options drive Roughness, Metallic, IOR, Transmission Weight, Coat Weight, Coat Roughness, Emission Color and Emission Strength. It produces a material resource, not geometry: every primitive needs one through its material input, and assignMaterial applies one to any processed or imported mesh. Every option has a Schemaxis default that is always assigned and read back from the shader, so an empty options object gives a mid-rough, non-metallic blue surface.
pitfalls: A material cannot be listed in a scene's visible or meshes; list the mesh that uses it.
A material that no selected mesh references is pruned and never created, so it is absent from the saved scene.
Colour values are linear shader values from 0 to 1, not sRGB hex codes; the PNG passes through Blender's colour management.
Mesh publications (scene meshes) are STL files, which do not carry materials.

cube.explanation: Creates a closed six-face cube mesh object with edge length size, centred on centre, using the material input. Schemaxis builds a fixed mesh spanning -1 to 1 on each local axis and realises size as the object's scale (size/2 on every axis) and centre as its location. Choose it for boxes, test parts and bevelled enclosures; for a non-cubic box follow it with transform scale, and use uvSphere, cylinder or the other primitives for other shapes.
pitfalls: Downstream modifiers (bevel width, solidify thickness, voxelSize, weld distance) act on the -1..1 local mesh, so they scale with size; insert applyTransform first when they must be in world units.
This is the operation in the recorded native qualification cases (signed volume 8 for size 2 and 27 for size 3).

bevel.explanation: Rounds or chamfers the edges of a copy of the input mesh with a Blender Bevel modifier (affect: edges) and produces a new mesh object with the input's world transform; the input object is unchanged. width and segments are assigned; the other Bevel settings keep Blender's new-modifier values, so width is the Offset of the new edges from the original edge and only edges whose faces meet more sharply than the 30 degree angle limit are bevelled. Follow it with shadeSmooth and weightedNormal for clean hard-surface shading.
pitfalls: width is in the input's local units; after cube or transform scaling the world bevel is larger or smaller. Use applyTransform before bevel to work in world units.
Gently curved regions (faces meeting at less than 30 degrees) are not bevelled by the native angle limit.

readGltf.explanation: Imports exactly one mesh object from a glTF 2.0 JSON file (.gltf) with Blender's glTF importer at its default settings; buffers and images must be embedded as data: URIs. Other imported objects are deleted, the mesh is unparented with its world transform kept, and imported materials stay on it. Use it to bring ParaView scene exports or other verified glTF artifacts into Blender; use readSTL or readPLY for those formats.
pitfalls: Binary .glb files, external .bin or image files, and documents with more than one mesh fail with UNSUPPORTED_RESOURCE.
glTF is a Y-up, metre-based format; the freecad-to-blender example applies transform rotation [-90, 0, 0] and scale 0.001 to restore a millimetre CAD part exported by ParaView.
The adaptor's recorded native qualification cases cover only a material on a cube; this operation relies on repository examples, not on a recorded qualification case.

lathe.explanation: Revolves a [radius, height] profile a full turn about the local Z axis to create a surface of revolution (vessels, nozzles, knobs), with optional flat caps at the first and last profile points. Schemaxis generates the quad mesh itself from the profile and segments, then applies the material, centre and smoothShading. Choose it when the shape is axisymmetric; use cylinder or cone for constant or linearly tapering sections.
pitfalls: Radii must be positive and heights must strictly increase; violations fail with INVALID_PROFILE at the profile's authored location during planning whenever the values are known host-side (literals, axes, times, expressions), and again when Blender builds the mesh; profiles that read native observations are checked only when Blender runs.
The adaptor's recorded native qualification cases cover only a material on a cube; this operation relies on repository examples, not on a recorded qualification case.

grid.explanation: Creates a flat rectangular grid of xSegments by ySegments quads in the local XY plane (z = 0), width along X and height along Y, centred on centre, with face normals along +Z. It is a single-sided surface with no thickness; choose it over plane when later deformation (bend, twist, shrinkwrap, smooth) needs interior vertices.
pitfalls: Add solidify when the grid must have a thickness or a closed volume.
The adaptor's recorded native qualification cases cover only a material on a cube; this operation relies on repository examples, not on a recorded qualification case.

disk.explanation: Creates a flat circular disk as one polygon whose segments vertices lie on a circle of the given radius in the local XY plane, centred on centre, with its normal along +Z. The polygon is inscribed in the circle, so its area is slightly smaller than pi r squared at low segment counts. Use it for end plates, markers and backdrops; use grid or subdivision when the face needs interior vertices.
pitfalls: The single n-gon has no interior vertices, so deforming it with bend or twist has little effect.
The adaptor's recorded native qualification cases cover only a material on a cube; this operation relies on repository examples, not on a recorded qualification case.

polylineTube.explanation: Sweeps a round tube of the given radius along straight segments between explicit 3D points, using a temporary native Blender POLY curve with a bevel that is converted to mesh and then discarded. Points are in the node's local coordinates and centre moves the whole tube. Choose it for pipes, wires, streamline-like paths or trajectories you can list inline; use curveFromCSV when the points come from a table.
pitfalls: Consecutive duplicate points create zero-length segments and fail with INVALID_GEOMETRY.
A closed tube needs at least three points.
The adaptor's recorded native qualification cases cover only a material on a cube; this operation relies on repository examples, not on a recorded qualification case.

curveFromCSV.explanation: Reads point coordinates from named columns of a numeric CSV table and sweeps the same round tube as polylineTube along them (rows in file order, 2 to 1024 rows). With zColumn empty the curve is planar at z = 0. The file is copied into the run directory and its SHA-256 digest is checked, so a measured or simulated trajectory becomes a reproducible presentation mesh.
pitfalls: Every cell of the CSV, including unused columns, must be a finite number under a UTF-8 header row; text columns fail with INVALID_TABLE.
Coordinates are used as Blender units without conversion; rescale with transform if the table is in millimetres.
The adaptor's recorded native qualification cases cover only a material on a cube; this operation relies on repository examples, not on a recorded qualification case.

plane.explanation: Creates a single rectangular quad of width (local X) by height (local Y) in the XY plane, centred on centre, with its normal along +Z. Use it for floors, backdrops and cutting or wrapping sheets; choose grid instead when the surface will be deformed, because a plane has only four vertices.
pitfalls: A plane has no thickness; add solidify before boolean or STL publication that needs a closed solid.
The adaptor's recorded native qualification cases cover only a material on a cube; this operation relies on repository examples, not on a recorded qualification case.

uvSphere.explanation: Creates a closed sphere mesh with Blender's bmesh UV-sphere generator: segments meridians around the local Z axis and rings latitude bands between the poles, all vertices on the given radius about centre. Faces crowd towards the poles; choose icoSphere for evenly sized triangles, for example before voxelRemesh or wireframe.
pitfalls: The mesh is inscribed in the true sphere, so its volume is below 4/3 pi r cubed; raise segments and rings when volume or silhouette accuracy matters.
The adaptor's recorded native qualification cases cover only a material on a cube; this operation relies on repository examples, not on a recorded qualification case.

icoSphere.explanation: Creates a closed sphere mesh by recursively subdividing an icosahedron with Blender's bmesh generator, giving near-uniform triangles with vertices on the given radius about centre. Choose it over uvSphere when even triangle size matters (wire cages, remeshing, deformation); subdivisions grows the face count by a factor of four per level.
pitfalls: Like uvSphere, the mesh is inscribed in the true sphere and slightly undersized in volume.
The adaptor's recorded native qualification cases cover only a material on a cube; this operation relies on repository examples, not on a recorded qualification case.

cylinder.explanation: Creates a closed, capped polygonal cylinder about the local Z axis with Blender's bmesh cone generator using the same radius at both ends; depth is the full height, centred on centre. The ends are single n-gon caps. Use cone for tapered sections and lathe for arbitrary axisymmetric profiles.
pitfalls: The axis is always local Z; use transform rotation to align it with another axis.
The adaptor's recorded native qualification cases cover only a material on a cube; this operation relies on repository examples, not on a recorded qualification case.

cone.explanation: Creates a capped cone or frustum about the local Z axis with Blender's bmesh cone generator: radius at the lower (-Z) end, tipRadius at the upper (+Z) end and depth as the full height, centred on centre. A tipRadius of 0 gives a pointed cone; a positive tipRadius gives a frustum such as a nozzle or diffuser section.
pitfalls: To point the tip downwards, rotate with transform (for example rotation [180, 0, 0]) rather than swapping radii.
The adaptor's recorded native qualification cases cover only a material on a cube; this operation relies on repository examples, not on a recorded qualification case.

torus.explanation: Creates a closed ring (torus) of quads lying in the local XY plane around the local Z axis: majorRadius is the distance from centre to the middle of the tube and minorRadius is the tube radius. majorSegments divides the ring and minorSegments divides the tube cross-section. Use it for O-rings, seals and annular markers.
pitfalls: Keep minorRadius below majorRadius; otherwise the tube passes through the axis and the surface self-intersects.
The adaptor's recorded native qualification cases cover only a material on a cube; this operation relies on repository examples, not on a recorded qualification case.

weld.explanation: Merges vertices of a copy of the input mesh that lie closer than distance, using Blender's Weld modifier in its default All mode. Use it after join, imports or array copies to fuse coincident seams so the surface becomes connected (important before solidify, smooth or STL publication of a watertight part). It removes duplicate vertices only; it does not fill gaps wider than distance.
pitfalls: distance is in the input's local units; a value close to real feature sizes collapses small details.
The adaptor's recorded native qualification cases cover only a material on a cube; this operation relies on repository examples, not on a recorded qualification case.

weightedNormal.explanation: Recomputes the shading normals of a copy of the input mesh with Blender's Weighted Normal modifier (native face area weighting), so large flat faces stay visually flat next to small bevel faces. It changes only the normals used for shading and rendering; vertex positions and topology are unchanged. Typical chain: bevel, shadeSmooth, weightedNormal.
pitfalls: STL mesh publications discard normals, so the effect appears only in rendered images and the saved scene.
This operation does not repair topology or holes.
The adaptor's recorded native qualification cases cover only a material on a cube; this operation relies on repository examples, not on a recorded qualification case.

voxelRemesh.explanation: Rebuilds a copy of the input mesh as a new surface from a voxelised volume using Blender's Remesh modifier in Voxel mode. The result is a single quad-dominant surface; overlapping joined parts fuse into one shell (a 'voxel union') and features smaller than voxelSize are lost. Schemaxis first rejects requests whose estimated bounding grid exceeds 8 million cells (RESOURCE_BUDGET_EXCEEDED).
pitfalls: voxelSize is in the input's local units; on a scaled object (cube size, transform scale) the world voxel size differs. Use applyTransform first.
The input should enclose a volume; open sheets produce thin or unexpected shells.
Topology, vertex count and fine detail change; do not use the result for dimensional checks finer than the voxel size.

bend.explanation: Bends a copy of the input mesh with Blender's Simple Deform modifier in Bend mode: the mesh is curved about the selected local axis by a total angle in radians spread over the mesh's extent. Other Simple Deform settings keep Blender's defaults (no origin object, full 0 to 1 limits), so the deformation is centred on the input object's local origin. Give the input enough vertices along the bend (subdivision method SIMPLE or grid) for a smooth curve.
pitfalls: angle is in radians, not degrees (1.5708 is a right-angle bend).
A cube or plane has too few vertices to bend smoothly; subdivide first.
Bending acts in local coordinates; bake transform scaling with applyTransform first when proportions matter.

twist.explanation: Twists a copy of the input mesh with Blender's Simple Deform modifier in Twist mode: cross-sections rotate about the selected local axis, accumulating the total angle (radians) over the mesh's extent along that axis, about the input object's local origin. Use it for twisted blades, helical shapes or parametric sweeps (the angle may be an $axis value). Subdivide the input along the axis first so the twist is resolved.
pitfalls: angle is in radians (6.2832 is one full turn).
Without intermediate vertices along the axis the faces only shear between the end loops.

shrinkwrap.explanation: Moves each vertex of a copy of the input mesh onto the surface of a second mesh, the target, using Blender's Shrinkwrap modifier with its default Nearest Surface Point method; mode decides how vertices may sit relative to the target and offset keeps a gap. Use it to drape a patch, label or coating onto another shape. The target is not changed and is rendered only if it is listed as visible.
pitfalls: The input needs enough vertices to follow curvature; subdivide a plane before wrapping.
Both meshes must be graph nodes; the target is resolved through its own transform in world space.
The adaptor's recorded native qualification cases cover only a material on a cube; this operation relies on repository examples, not on a recorded qualification case.

wireframe.explanation: Turns every edge of a copy of the input mesh into a solid strut of the given thickness using Blender's Wireframe modifier; replace removes the original faces and boundary also builds struts along open edges. Use it to show a mesh's tessellation or to create lattice-like presentation geometry; triangulate first for a triangle cage.
pitfalls: A triangle wireframe shows tessellation, not physical structure such as flow features.
thickness is in the input's local units and is scaled by the input object's transform.

solidify.explanation: Gives a copy of the input surface a uniform shell thickness with Blender's Solidify modifier (Simple extrusion mode, rims on); offset places the shell inside, centred on or outside the original surface relative to its normals. Use it to turn sheets (plane, grid, wrapped or imported surfaces) into closed panels or shells that can be rendered with thickness, published as solid STL or used in boolean.
pitfalls: thickness is in the input's local units; a scaled input yields a different world thickness.
Inconsistent face normals make the shell grow in different directions; check normals of imported meshes.
The adaptor's recorded native qualification cases cover only a material on a cube; this operation relies on repository examples, not on a recorded qualification case.

subdivision.explanation: Subdivides a copy of the input mesh with Blender's Subdivision Surface modifier; Schemaxis sets the same level for viewport and render evaluation, so images, saved scenes and STL publications agree. CATMULL_CLARK smooths and rounds the shape; SIMPLE only adds vertices and keeps the shape, which is the usual preparation for bend, twist, shrinkwrap or smooth.
pitfalls: Each level multiplies the face count by about four; level 4 on a detailed import can be very large.
CATMULL_CLARK shrinks sharp shapes such as a cube towards a rounded blob; add bevel first or use SIMPLE.

decimate.explanation: Reduces the polygon count of a copy of the input mesh with Blender's Decimate modifier in its default Collapse mode, keeping approximately ratio of the triangles. Use it to lighten heavy imports or remeshed surfaces for rendering or publication; geometric detail and sharp edges can be lost.
pitfalls: The Schemaxis default ratio 0.5 halves the triangles even when you only wanted to add the node; set 1 to keep everything.
Do not use decimated geometry for measurements that need the original surface.
The adaptor's recorded native qualification cases cover only a material on a cube; this operation relies on repository examples, not on a recorded qualification case.

triangulate.explanation: Splits every quad and n-gon of a copy of the input mesh into triangles with Blender's Triangulate modifier at its default settings (quads along the shortest diagonal, n-gons by the Beauty method). Use it before wireframe for a triangle cage or to control how polygons are split before export; it has no options.
pitfalls: STL publication triangulates anyway; add this node only when the triangle layout itself matters.
The adaptor's recorded native qualification cases cover only a material on a cube; this operation relies on repository examples, not on a recorded qualification case.

smooth.explanation: Relaxes vertex positions of a copy of the input mesh with Blender's Smooth modifier, moving each vertex towards its neighbours by factor for a number of iterations on all three axes; topology is unchanged. Use it to soften noisy scans or faceted imports. Repeated smoothing shrinks the shape and rounds corners.
pitfalls: A cube or other low-vertex mesh collapses quickly; subdivide first or use shadeSmooth when only the shading should look smooth.
The adaptor's recorded native qualification cases cover only a material on a cube; this operation relies on repository examples, not on a recorded qualification case.

array.explanation: Repeats the input mesh count times in one new mesh with Blender's Array modifier, each copy offset by relativeOffset times the input's bounding-box size along each local axis (relative offset on, constant offset and vertex merging off, as in a new Blender modifier). Use it for regular rows of blades, fins, bolts or test specimens.
pitfalls: count includes the original; count 1 produces no copies.
Copies touching at relativeOffset 1 are not merged; add weld if they must be connected.
The adaptor's recorded native qualification cases cover only a material on a cube; this operation relies on repository examples, not on a recorded qualification case.

mirror.explanation: Adds the reflection of a copy of the input mesh across the selected local axis planes with Blender's Mirror modifier; the planes pass through the input object's local origin, and merge welds vertices that land on the mirror plane (Blender's 0.001 merge distance). Use it to model one half or quarter of a symmetric part and complete it.
pitfalls: Primitives have their origin at centre, so mirroring a whole primitive overlaps it with itself; model only one side of the plane.
To mirror about a world plane after transform, insert applyTransform so the local origin is the world origin.
The adaptor's recorded native qualification cases cover only a material on a cube; this operation relies on repository examples, not on a recorded qualification case.

boolean.explanation: Combines the input mesh with a second mesh, the operand, using Blender's Boolean modifier with the Exact solver: DIFFERENCE cuts the operand away, UNION merges both volumes and INTERSECT keeps only the overlap. The result is a new mesh object; the operand is unchanged and is rendered only if listed as visible. Use it for holes, cut-aways and section views.
pitfalls: Both meshes should be closed, consistently oriented volumes; open sheets give unreliable results (solidify them first).
Coplanar faces are handled by the Exact solver but are slow on dense meshes; offset the operand slightly when possible.
The adaptor's recorded native qualification cases cover only a material on a cube; this operation relies on repository examples, not on a recorded qualification case.

assignMaterial.explanation: Copies the evaluated input mesh (with its world transform) and replaces all of its material slots with the single material input on every face. The upstream object and its materials stay unchanged, so the same geometry can be styled differently for several presentations. Use it for imported or processed meshes, which have no material input of their own.
pitfalls: Per-face material assignments from join or imports are lost; every face gets this material.

applyTransform.explanation: Bakes the input object's world transform (location, rotation and scale from centre, cube size or transform) into the vertex coordinates of a copy and resets the object transform to identity. The world-space shape is unchanged, but later modifiers then act on world-sized geometry about the world origin. Insert it before bevel, solidify, voxelRemesh, bend, twist or mirror when their sizes, axes or planes must refer to world units.
pitfalls: It does not move anything visibly; compare modifier results with and without it when proportions look wrong.
The adaptor's recorded native qualification cases cover only a material on a cube; this operation relies on repository examples, not on a recorded qualification case.

shadeSmooth.explanation: Copies the input mesh and sets every face to smooth (enabled true) or flat (enabled false) shading. Smooth shading interpolates normals across faces so tessellated curved surfaces render without facets; positions and topology are unchanged. Use subdivision or smooth when the geometry itself must change.
pitfalls: Smooth shading on hard-edged parts creates dark gradients; follow with weightedNormal or bevel the edges.
STL publications do not carry shading flags.

join.explanation: Combines the evaluated geometry of two or more mesh nodes into one mesh in world coordinates (the result has an identity transform), keeping each face's material and smooth flag. It only gathers faces: overlapping parts remain separate intersecting shells, unlike a boolean UNION. Follow with weld to fuse touching seams or voxelRemesh to fuse overlaps into one surface.
pitfalls: UV maps, vertex groups, custom attributes and custom normals are not preserved.
The adaptor's recorded native qualification cases cover only a material on a cube; this operation relies on repository examples, not on a recorded qualification case.

readSTL.explanation: Imports one triangle mesh from an STL file with Blender's STL importer, multiplying coordinates by scale and keeping the file's axes (Y forward, Z up, scene units ignored). STL carries no unit information, so scale is how you convert: 0.001 turns a millimetre CAD export into metre-sized Blender units. The file is copied into the run directory and its digest checked.
pitfalls: The file must produce exactly one mesh object with faces; otherwise UNSUPPORTED_RESOURCE.
scale is a constant set at creation; it cannot vary with an $axis. Use transform for varying scale.
The adaptor's recorded native qualification cases cover only a material on a cube; this operation relies on repository examples, not on a recorded qualification case.

readPLY.explanation: Imports one polygon mesh from a PLY file with Blender's PLY importer, multiplying coordinates by scale and keeping the file's axes (Y forward, Z up, scene units ignored); other importer options keep Blender's defaults. PLY carries no unit information, so scale converts units. Point-only PLY files are rejected because the mesh must have faces.
pitfalls: A point cloud PLY fails with UNSUPPORTED_RESOURCE; mesh it elsewhere first.
scale is a constant set at creation; it cannot vary with an $axis.
The adaptor's recorded native qualification cases cover only a material on a cube; this operation relies on repository examples, not on a recorded qualification case.

transform.explanation: Places a copy of the input mesh by composing translation, rotation (XYZ Euler, degrees) and scale on top of the input object's world transform: world = T * R * S * input. Scale and rotation therefore act about the world origin, not the part's own centre. The mesh vertices are not changed; only the object transform is, so later modifiers still work in the original local coordinates unless you add applyTransform.
pitfalls: A part centred away from the origin moves when scaled or rotated; translate it to the origin first or apply the transform before it is offset.
Rotation is in degrees here, whereas bend and twist angles are radians.

fields.explanation: Structural schema after document composition, inline objects and analytics expansion. Run Schemaxis plan/run for reference, dependency, cross-option, expression-result and native validation.

/properties/version.explanation: Identifies the document format and chooses its adaptor. Keep the version matching the selected schema.

/properties/nodes.explanation: The scene graph: material nodes, mesh sources (primitives and readers) and mesh operations connected through their inputs by node id. Schemaxis orders them by dependency, not by list position, and creates only nodes needed by the scene's visible, meshes or camera observations; unreferenced nodes are pruned. Ids must be unique.
/properties/nodes.label: Nodes
pitfalls: A node that no visible or meshes entry depends on is not created and does not appear in the saved scene.
Dependency cycles fail with PIPELINE_CYCLE.

/properties/scenes.explanation: The scene to prepare and publish. The Blender adaptor requires exactly one scene; for every state it frames the cameras, renders images (unless prepareOnly), exports the listed meshes and saves a .blend file.
/properties/scenes.label: Scenes

/properties/scenes/items.explanation: One scene: which meshes are rendered, how, from which cameras, and which meshes are also published as STL. Per state the artifacts are ordered: all images (camera order), then the meshes in listed order, then the saved .blend, which a schemaxis.blender.render/1 job can render again later.

/properties/scenes/items/properties/id.explanation: Give this object a unique name. References use this name to identify the result or object.

/properties/scenes/items/properties/visi.explanation: Mesh node ids that are rendered; every other created object is hidden from rendering but still saved in the .blend. Together they also define the default camera framing bounds (their union). At least one id; material nodes are not allowed.
/properties/scenes/items/properties/visi.label: Visible meshes
pitfalls: Inputs, operands and targets of later operations are still created and saved but do not appear in images unless listed; list only final results to avoid overlapping copies in the picture.
Listing a material fails with TYPE_MISMATCH.

/properties/scenes/items/properties/visi.explanation: Id of one mesh-producing node to render. Its world bounds join the framing bounds.

/properties/scenes/items/properties/rend.explanation: Cycles render settings, world lighting and the single area light used for every image of this scene and stored in the saved .blend. Omitted keys take the Schemaxis defaults shown on each field; samples, denoise and the light most affect image quality.

Cycles compute backend. CPU renders anywhere and is the reproducible baseline. CUDA (NVIDIA GPUs) or OPTIX (NVIDIA RTX ray-tracing hardware) are faster for many samples; Schemaxis enables only devices of that type, reserves one GPU in workflow scheduling and fails verification unless the device use is evidenced.
/properties/scenes/items/properties/rend.label: Render device
pitfalls: A GPU backend that the machine or driver lacks fails with DEVICE_UNAVAILABLE.
GPU and CPU renders of the same scene are not guaranteed to be pixel-identical.

/properties/scenes/items/properties/rend.explanation: Cycles samples per pixel (scene.cycles.samples). More samples reduce noise roughly with the square root of the count but cost proportional time; the default is a quick preview. Transmission, emission and small lights need more.
/properties/scenes/items/properties/rend.label: Samples

/properties/scenes/items/properties/rend.explanation: Fixed number of CPU threads for rendering (render threads mode FIXED). In workflows the operation's execution threads must equal this value, so the scheduler reserves exactly what Blender uses.
/properties/scenes/items/properties/rend.label: Render threads
pitfalls: A workflow execution.threads that differs fails with INVALID_EXECUTION; set both together.

/properties/scenes/items/properties/rend.explanation: When true Cycles denoises the final image (use_denoising), giving clean images from few samples at the cost of slightly smoothed fine texture; when false the raw sampled noise remains.
/properties/scenes/items/properties/rend.label: Denoise

/properties/scenes/items/properties/rend.explanation: When true the world background is rendered transparent (film_transparent) for compositing over another background; the world colour still lights the model. When false the background shows worldColour.
/properties/scenes/items/properties/rend.label: Transparent background

/properties/scenes/items/properties/rend.explanation: Cycles sampling seed. The same seed and settings reproduce the same noise pattern; changing it gives a different but statistically equivalent noise, useful to check whether a feature is noise.
/properties/scenes/items/properties/rend.label: Seed

/properties/scenes/items/properties/rend.explanation: Colour [red, green, blue] of the uniform world background (Background shader), 0 to 1. It is both the visible background and an ambient light from all directions, so it tints the model as well.
/properties/scenes/items/properties/rend.label: World colour

/properties/scenes/items/properties/rend.explanation: One channel of the world colour: index 0 red, 1 green, 2 blue, from 0 to 1.
Strength of the world background light. Higher values brighten the background and fill shadows evenly; 0 leaves only the area light (and emission), giving a black background and high contrast.
/properties/scenes/items/properties/rend.label: World strength

/properties/scenes/items/properties/rend.explanation: Radiant power of the single square area light that Schemaxis adds (Blender light energy). The illumination reaching the model falls with the square of the distance from lightPosition, so rescale energy when the model or the light is moved much nearer or farther.
/properties/scenes/items/properties/rend.label: Light power
pitfalls: Small parts lit from a nearby lightPosition need far less energy (the freecad-to-blender example uses 20 W at about 0.4 units).

/properties/scenes/items/properties/rend.explanation: World position [x, y, z] of the area light. The light is always aimed at the world origin, not at the model, so for models far from the origin move it accordingly (or move the model to the origin).
/properties/scenes/items/properties/rend.label: Light position
/properties/scenes/items/properties/rend.units: Blender units (scene world units; Schemaxis applies no unit conversion)
/properties/scenes/items/properties/rend.defaultMeaning: Schemaxis default: [4, -4, 6] (front-right, above, about 8.2 units from the origin).

/properties/scenes/items/properties/rend.explanation: One world coordinate of the light position: index 0 is x, 1 is y, 2 is z.
/properties/scenes/items/properties/rend.units: Blender units (scene world units; Schemaxis applies no unit conversion)

/properties/scenes/items/properties/rend.explanation: Edge length of the square area light. Larger lights give softer shadow edges; smaller ones give crisper shadows and highlights.
/properties/scenes/items/properties/rend.label: Light size
/properties/scenes/items/properties/rend.units: Blender units (scene world units; Schemaxis applies no unit conversion)

/properties/scenes/items/properties/prep.explanation: When true the scene is built, cameras are framed and the .blend (and any meshes) are published for each state, but no images are rendered; the camera stored in the .blend is the last one in the list. Use it to prepare a scene once and render it later with one or more schemaxis.blender.render/1 jobs.
/properties/scenes/items/properties/prep.label: Prepare only
/properties/scenes/items/properties/prep.defaultMeaning: false: images are rendered for every camera.

/properties/scenes/items/properties/mesh.explanation: Mesh node ids whose evaluated geometry is published as a binary STL per state ({state}-{node}.stl), in world coordinates and Blender units, after a native export/import round trip check. Use it to hand processed geometry to another workflow operation (ParaView, another Blender job). Nodes need not be visible.
/properties/scenes/items/properties/mesh.label: Published meshes
/properties/scenes/items/properties/mesh.defaultMeaning: None: no STL files are published.
pitfalls: STL loses materials, normals, UVs, attributes and unit metadata.
Each mesh is limited to one million triangles.

/properties/scenes/items/properties/mesh.explanation: Id of one mesh node to publish; ids must be distinct, and their order is the artifact order.

/properties/scenes/items/properties/imag.explanation: Image writer for the scene; exactly one writer is accepted. Its cameras decide how many PNGs each state produces.
/properties/scenes/items/properties/imag.label: Images

/properties/scenes/items/properties/imag.explanation: One image writer: an id, a pixel size shared by all its cameras, and the camera list. Each camera renders {state}-{camera}.png in the run directory.
Give this object a unique name. References use this name to identify the result or object.
Output image size [width, height] in pixels, each 32 to 2048. The aspect ratio also affects the automatic orthographic width (it widens with width/height).
/properties/scenes/items/properties/imag.label: Image size

/properties/scenes/items/properties/imag.explanation: One image dimension in pixels: index 0 is the width, index 1 the height (32 to 2048).
Camera views rendered for every state, in list order. It may also be an $analytic orbit sequence, which expands into one camera per azimuth.
/properties/scenes/items/properties/imag.label: Cameras

/properties/scenes/items/properties/imag.explanation: One camera view. Each camera produces one PNG per state (unless prepareOnly), framed on the bounds of the scene's visible meshes in the current state unless bounds, focalPoint, scale or distance are given. Omitted settings mean: view from +x, Z up, orthographic, automatic fit with 10% padding. Values may be runtime expressions, for example bounds from $observe.

Which side of the subject the camera looks from: Blender places the camera at focalPoint + unit(direction) x distance and points it back at the focal point. "x+" or [1, 0, 0] views from +x; [1, -2, 1] gives a raised front-right view. Give an axis token, a vector, or an azimuth/elevation object.
/properties/scenes/items/properties/imag.label: View direction
pitfalls: It must not be parallel to up; for views straight down use direction "z+" with up "y+".

/properties/scenes/items/properties/imag.explanation: Which side of the subject the camera looks from: Blender places the camera at focalPoint + unit(direction) x distance and points it back at the focal point. "x+" or [1, 0, 0] views from +x; [1, -2, 1] gives a raised front-right view. Give an axis token, a vector, or an azimuth/elevation object.
pitfalls: It must not be parallel to up; for views straight down use direction "z+" with up "y+".

/properties/scenes/items/properties/imag.explanation: Axis-token spelling: names a world axis and sign, e.g. "x+", "y-" or "z+" (also "x", "+x", "xp", "xm", "-x"; case-insensitive). Choose it for directions along world axes, such as standard front, side or top views; here the token gives the side of the subject the camera is placed on: Blender puts the camera at focalPoint + direction x distance, looking back at the focal point.
pitfalls: A camera direction of "z+" or "z-" is parallel to the default up [0, 0, 1] and fails with INVALID_CAMERA; set up to "y+" for top or bottom views.

/properties/scenes/items/properties/imag.explanation: Axis-token spelling: names a world axis and sign, e.g. "x+", "y-" or "z+" (also "x", "+x", "xp", "xm", "-x"; case-insensitive). Choose it for directions along world axes, such as standard front, side or top views; here the token gives the side of the subject the camera is placed on: Blender puts the camera at focalPoint + direction x distance, looking back at the focal point.
pitfalls: A camera direction of "z+" or "z-" is parallel to the default up [0, 0, 1] and fails with INVALID_CAMERA; set up to "y+" for top or bottom views.

/properties/scenes/items/properties/imag.explanation: A runtime expression: a JSON object that replaces a whole option or camera value and is evaluated for each state after upstream nodes are updated. In Blender documents it can read an axis value ($axis), the time ($time) or an updated node's observation ($observe), and combine them with $calc arithmetic or registered $call functions. The result must still satisfy the destination field. Constructor settings (reader file and scale, curveFromCSV file) cannot use it, and field sampling ($sample) is not available in Blender.

Vector spelling [x, y, z] in world axes; only its direction matters, Schemaxis normalises it. Choose it for oblique views or directions computed elsewhere; here it gives the side of the subject the camera is placed on: Blender puts the camera at focalPoint + direction x distance, looking back at the focal point.
pitfalls: [0, 0, 0] has no direction and is rejected.

/properties/scenes/items/properties/imag.explanation: Vector spelling [x, y, z] in world axes; only its direction matters, Schemaxis normalises it. Choose it for oblique views or directions computed elsewhere; here it gives the side of the subject the camera is placed on: Blender puts the camera at focalPoint + direction x distance, looking back at the focal point.
pitfalls: [0, 0, 0] has no direction and is rejected.

/properties/scenes/items/properties/imag.explanation: One world-axis component of the direction vector: index 0 is x, 1 is y, 2 is z. Only the ratios between components matter.
One world-axis component of the direction vector: index 0 is x, 1 is y, 2 is z. Only the ratios between components matter.

The result must still satisfy the destination field. Constructor settings (reader file and scale, curveFromCSV file) cannot use it, and field sampling ($sample) is not available in Blender.

Fractional margin for automatic orthographic framing: the shorter image side spans (1 + padding) times the bounds diagonal, so 0.1 leaves roughly 10% of extra room. Ignored when scale is set or parallel is false.
/properties/scenes/items/properties/imag.label: Padding

/properties/axes.explanation: Named parameter axes for studies. Each axis lists values; options or cameras read the current value with {"$axis": name}. Only axes actually used by created nodes are active, and every combination of active axis values (first listed axis varies fastest) and times is one state with its own images, meshes and .blend.
/properties/axes.label: Axes
pitfalls: An axis used only by a camera, not by any node option, is inactive and fails with UNKNOWN_AXIS.
States multiply: three axes of ten values give a thousand renders.

/properties/axes/items.explanation: One axis: a unique name plus either explicit values or a linear series of positions.

/properties/axes/items/properties/name.explanation: Name referenced by {"$axis": name} markers; letters, digits, underscore and hyphen, starting with a letter, unique within the document.
/properties/axes/items/properties/name.label: Axis name

/properties/axes/items/properties/values.explanation: Values the axis takes, one state per value in list order. A value may be any JSON (number, vector, object); markers can select parts of it with path.
/properties/axes/items/properties/values.label: Values

/properties/axes/items/properties/values.explanation: Free JSON data used by axis values and the definitions, dimensions, views and settings containers. Schemaxis does not interpret it there; it becomes meaningful when $document markers copy parts of it into fields, or when $axis reads axis values.

/properties/axes/items/properties/series.explanation: Positions along an axis, given as any three of start, end, spacing and count
First position; defaults to the padded lower bound
Last position; defaults to the padded upper bound
Absolute inset applied to bounds-derived ends only
Inset as a fraction of the bounds extent, applied to bounds-derived ends only

/properties/axes/items/oneOf/0.explanation: Explicit-values form: the axis lists its values directly. Choose it for arbitrary or non-uniform values, or non-numeric values such as vectors.

/properties/axes/items/oneOf/0/not.explanation: Rule of the explicit-values form: series must not be given together with values.

/properties/axes/items/oneOf/1.explanation: Series form: positions are generated from any three of start, end, spacing and count. Choose it for evenly spaced numeric sweeps. Blender axes have no bounds to derive missing ends from, so declare exactly three of start, end, spacing and count yourself.

/properties/axes/items/oneOf/1/not.explanation: Rule of the series form: values must not be given together with series.

/properties/times.explanation: Time values visited in order; each multiplies the number of states. Blender operations have no time-dependent data, so times matter only where options read {"$time": true}; every node is updated when the time changes.
/properties/times.label: Times

/properties/times/items.explanation: One time value; finite number, returned unchanged by $time. Order is the visiting order.

/properties/definitions.explanation: Free JSON data used by axis values and the definitions, dimensions, views and settings containers. Schemaxis does not interpret it there; it becomes meaningful when $document markers copy parts of it into fields, or when $axis reads axis values.

/properties/dimensions.explanation: Free JSON data used by axis values and the definitions, dimensions, views and settings containers. Schemaxis does not interpret it there; it becomes meaningful when $document markers copy parts of it into fields, or when $axis reads axis values.

/properties/views.explanation: Free JSON data used by axis values and the definitions, dimensions, views and settings containers. Schemaxis does not interpret it there; it becomes meaningful when $document markers copy parts of it into fields, or when $axis reads axis values.

/properties/settings.explanation: Free JSON data used by axis values and the definitions, dimensions, views and settings containers. Schemaxis does not interpret it there; it becomes meaningful when $document markers copy parts of it into fields, or when $axis reads axis values.

/properties/maxStates.explanation: Upper limit on states (active axis combinations times times, and series positions). Planning fails with EXPANSION_TOO_LARGE above it, protecting against accidental huge sweeps.
/properties/maxStates.label: Maximum states

/properties/maxPublications.explanation: Upper limit on published artifacts: states x (cameras + 1 .blend, or just the .blend with prepareOnly, + published meshes). Planning fails with EXPANSION_TOO_LARGE above it.
/properties/maxPublications.label: Maximum publications

/$defs/runtime.explanation: A runtime expression: a JSON object that replaces a whole option or camera value and is evaluated for each state after upstream nodes are updated. In Blender documents it can read an axis value ($axis), the time ($time) or an updated node's observation ($observe), and combine them with $calc arithmetic or registered $call functions. The result must still satisfy the destination field. Constructor settings (reader file and scale, curveFromCSV file) cannot use it, and field sampling ($sample) is not available in Blender.

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/0.explanation: Reads the current state's value of a declared axis. Choose it to sweep a setting over the values of an axis, one state per value; path selects a part of a structured value.

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/0/properties/$axis.explanation: Name of an axis declared under axes. Using it in a node option makes that axis active; an undeclared or inactive name fails with UNKNOWN_AXIS.
/$defs/runtime/anyOf/0/properties/$axis.label: Axis name

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/0/properties/path.explanation: Steps into the axis value, applied in order: a string selects an object key, an integer a zero-based list index. For an axis of [x, y, z] vectors, [2] reads z.
/$defs/runtime/anyOf/0/properties/path.label: Path

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/0/properties/path/i.explanation: One step of the path; an object key (string) or a zero-based list index (integer).
An object key, used when the axis values are JSON objects; it must exist in the selected value.
A zero-based list index, used when the selected value is an array (for example 0 for x of a vector).

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/1.explanation: Reads metadata Blender observed on an upstream node after it was updated in the current state, and makes this node depend on it. Mesh nodes report bounds (world [xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax, zmin, zmax]), signedVolume, points, cells, transform (4x4 world matrix rows) and geometrySha256; material nodes report their shader values such as colour, roughness and metallic. Choose it to place or size one object from another, or to aim cameras at a node.

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/1/properties/$obser.explanation: Id of the node to observe. It becomes a dependency (created and updated first) even if it is not visible; in a camera it must belong to the active graph.
/$defs/runtime/anyOf/1/properties/$obser.label: Observed node

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/1/properties/path.explanation: Steps into the observation: ["bounds"] gives the six-number world bounds, ["bounds", 4] its zmin, ["signedVolume"] the enclosed volume of a mesh in cubic Blender units.
/$defs/runtime/anyOf/1/properties/path.label: Path
pitfalls: Bounds are min/max per axis; index 1 is xmax, not ymin.

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/1/properties/path/i.explanation: One step into the observation: a key such as "bounds" or a zero-based index into an array.
An observation key: for meshes kind, bounds, signedVolume, points, cells, transform or geometrySha256.
A zero-based index into an array in the observation, such as a bounds position (0 to 5) or a transform row.

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/2.explanation: Returns the current time from the document's times list. Choose it to make an option follow time across states; Blender itself has no time-dependent data.

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/2/properties/$time.explanation: Must be exactly true; any other value fails with INVALID_EXPRESSION.
/$defs/runtime/anyOf/2/properties/$time.label: Time marker

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/3.explanation: Runtime calculation "vector": Builds an [x, y, z] vector from three finite scalar arguments, each of which may itself be an expression; use it to vary one component of a centre, translation or direction. Results must be finite.
pitfalls: Each argument must evaluate to a single finite number.

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/3/properties/$calc.explanation: Selects the "vector" calculation; it is fixed for this form.
/$defs/runtime/anyOf/3/properties/$calc.label: Calculation

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/3/properties/args.explanation: Arguments of "vector": three scalar arguments: x, y and z. Each may be a literal or another runtime expression and is evaluated before the calculation.
/$defs/runtime/anyOf/3/properties/args.label: Arguments

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/3/properties/args/i.explanation: One $calc argument: a literal number, string, boolean or null, an array of such values (for example a vector), or a nested runtime expression.

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/4.explanation: Runtime calculation "midpoint": Centre [x, y, z] of six-number bounds [xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax, zmin, zmax], such as an observed mesh's bounds. Results must be finite.
pitfalls: Bounds with a minimum greater than its maximum fail with INVALID_BOUNDS.

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/4/properties/$calc.explanation: Selects the "midpoint" calculation; it is fixed for this form.
/$defs/runtime/anyOf/4/properties/$calc.label: Calculation

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/4/properties/args.explanation: Arguments of "midpoint": one argument: six-number bounds. Each may be a literal or another runtime expression and is evaluated before the calculation.
/$defs/runtime/anyOf/4/properties/args.label: Arguments

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/4/properties/args/i.explanation: One $calc argument: a literal number, string, boolean or null, an array of such values (for example a vector), or a nested runtime expression.

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/5.explanation: Runtime calculation "boundsMin": Lower corner [xmin, ymin, zmin] of six-number bounds. Results must be finite.
pitfalls: Bounds with a minimum greater than its maximum fail with INVALID_BOUNDS.

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/5/properties/$calc.explanation: Selects the "boundsMin" calculation; it is fixed for this form.
/$defs/runtime/anyOf/5/properties/$calc.label: Calculation

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/5/properties/args.explanation: Arguments of "boundsMin": one argument: six-number bounds. Each may be a literal or another runtime expression and is evaluated before the calculation.
/$defs/runtime/anyOf/5/properties/args.label: Arguments

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/5/properties/args/i.explanation: One $calc argument: a literal number, string, boolean or null, an array of such values (for example a vector), or a nested runtime expression.

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/6.explanation: Runtime calculation "boundsMax": Upper corner [xmax, ymax, zmax] of six-number bounds. Results must be finite.
pitfalls: Bounds with a minimum greater than its maximum fail with INVALID_BOUNDS.

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/6/properties/$calc.explanation: Selects the "boundsMax" calculation; it is fixed for this form.
/$defs/runtime/anyOf/6/properties/$calc.label: Calculation

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/6/properties/args.explanation: Arguments of "boundsMax": one argument: six-number bounds. Each may be a literal or another runtime expression and is evaluated before the calculation.
/$defs/runtime/anyOf/6/properties/args.label: Arguments

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/6/properties/args/i.explanation: One $calc argument: a literal number, string, boolean or null, an array of such values (for example a vector), or a nested runtime expression.

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/7.explanation: Runtime calculation "add": Sum of two scalars, two equal-length vectors (element by element) or a vector and a scalar (broadcast). Results must be finite.
pitfalls: Vectors of different lengths cannot be combined; booleans and strings are rejected.

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/7/properties/$calc.explanation: Selects the "add" calculation; it is fixed for this form.
/$defs/runtime/anyOf/7/properties/$calc.label: Calculation

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/7/properties/args.explanation: Arguments of "add": two arguments to add. Each may be a literal or another runtime expression and is evaluated before the calculation.
/$defs/runtime/anyOf/7/properties/args.label: Arguments

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/7/properties/args/i.explanation: One $calc argument: a literal number, string, boolean or null, an array of such values (for example a vector), or a nested runtime expression.

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/8.explanation: Runtime calculation "subtract": First argument minus the second, for scalars, equal-length vectors or a vector and a scalar. Results must be finite.
pitfalls: Vectors of different lengths cannot be combined; booleans and strings are rejected.

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/8/properties/$calc.explanation: Selects the "subtract" calculation; it is fixed for this form.
/$defs/runtime/anyOf/8/properties/$calc.label: Calculation

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/8/properties/args.explanation: Arguments of "subtract": two arguments: minuend then subtrahend. Each may be a literal or another runtime expression and is evaluated before the calculation.
/$defs/runtime/anyOf/8/properties/args.label: Arguments

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/8/properties/args/i.explanation: One $calc argument: a literal number, string, boolean or null, an array of such values (for example a vector), or a nested runtime expression.

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/9.explanation: Runtime calculation "multiply": Product of two scalars, element-by-element product of equal-length vectors, or a vector scaled by a scalar. Results must be finite.
pitfalls: Vectors of different lengths cannot be combined; booleans and strings are rejected.

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/9/properties/$calc.explanation: Selects the "multiply" calculation; it is fixed for this form.
/$defs/runtime/anyOf/9/properties/$calc.label: Calculation

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/9/properties/args.explanation: Arguments of "multiply": two factors. Each may be a literal or another runtime expression and is evaluated before the calculation.
/$defs/runtime/anyOf/9/properties/args.label: Arguments

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/9/properties/args/i.explanation: One $calc argument: a literal number, string, boolean or null, an array of such values (for example a vector), or a nested runtime expression.

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/10.explanation: Runtime calculation "divide": First argument divided by the second, for scalars, equal-length vectors or a vector and a scalar; division by zero fails. Results must be finite.
pitfalls: Vectors of different lengths cannot be combined; booleans and strings are rejected.

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/10/properties/$calc.explanation: Selects the "divide" calculation; it is fixed for this form.
/$defs/runtime/anyOf/10/properties/$calc.label: Calculation

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/10/properties/args.explanation: Arguments of "divide": two arguments: dividend then divisor. Each may be a literal or another runtime expression and is evaluated before the calculation.
/$defs/runtime/anyOf/10/properties/args.label: Arguments

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/10/properties/args/.explanation: One $calc argument: a literal number, string, boolean or null, an array of such values (for example a vector), or a nested runtime expression.

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/11.explanation: Runtime calculation "min": Smaller of two scalars, or the element-by-element minimum of vectors. Results must be finite.
pitfalls: Vectors of different lengths cannot be combined; booleans and strings are rejected.

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/11/properties/$calc.explanation: Selects the "min" calculation; it is fixed for this form.
/$defs/runtime/anyOf/11/properties/$calc.label: Calculation

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/11/properties/args.explanation: Arguments of "min": two arguments to compare. Each may be a literal or another runtime expression and is evaluated before the calculation.
/$defs/runtime/anyOf/11/properties/args.label: Arguments

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/11/properties/args/.explanation: One $calc argument: a literal number, string, boolean or null, an array of such values (for example a vector), or a nested runtime expression.

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/12.explanation: Runtime calculation "max": Larger of two scalars, or the element-by-element maximum of vectors. Results must be finite.
pitfalls: Vectors of different lengths cannot be combined; booleans and strings are rejected.

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/12/properties/$calc.explanation: Selects the "max" calculation; it is fixed for this form.
/$defs/runtime/anyOf/12/properties/$calc.label: Calculation

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/12/properties/args.explanation: Arguments of "max": two arguments to compare. Each may be a literal or another runtime expression and is evaluated before the calculation.
/$defs/runtime/anyOf/12/properties/args.label: Arguments

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/12/properties/args/.explanation: One $calc argument: a literal number, string, boolean or null, an array of such values (for example a vector), or a nested runtime expression.

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/13.explanation: Calls boundsCentre: the centre [x, y, z] of six-number bounds. It accepts observed Blender bounds directly, so it is the simplest way to aim a camera's focalPoint or place a centre at another mesh's middle.

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/13/properties/$call.explanation: Selects the registered function boundsCentre; it is fixed for this form.
/$defs/runtime/anyOf/13/properties/$call.label: Function

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/13/properties/args.explanation: Arguments of boundsCentre: bounds, the six-number box whose centre is returned.
/$defs/runtime/anyOf/13/properties/args.label: Arguments

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/13/properties/args/.explanation: Six numbers [xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax, zmin, zmax], typically {"$observe": node, "path": ["bounds"]}.
/$defs/runtime/anyOf/13/properties/args/.label: Bounds
/$defs/runtime/anyOf/13/properties/args/.units: Blender units (scene world units; Schemaxis applies no unit conversion)
pitfalls: Any minimum above its maximum fails with FUNCTION_FAILED.

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/13/properties/args/.explanation: Six numbers [xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax, zmin, zmax], typically {"$observe": node, "path": ["bounds"]}.
/$defs/runtime/anyOf/13/properties/args/.units: Blender units (scene world units; Schemaxis applies no unit conversion)
pitfalls: Any minimum above its maximum fails with FUNCTION_FAILED.

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/13/properties/args/.explanation: One bound value; positions 0 to 5 are xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax, zmin, zmax.
/$defs/runtime/anyOf/13/properties/args/.units: Blender units (scene world units; Schemaxis applies no unit conversion)

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/13/properties/args/.explanation: One bound value; positions 0 to 5 are xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax, zmin, zmax.
/$defs/runtime/anyOf/13/properties/args/.units: Blender units (scene world units; Schemaxis applies no unit conversion)

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/14.explanation: Calls boundsCentre3D: the centre [x, y, z] of a {min, max} box. Use boundsCentre instead when you have six-number bounds from $observe.

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/14/properties/args.explanation: Arguments of boundsCentre3D: bounds, the {min, max} box.

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/14/properties/args/.explanation: Axis-aligned box as {"min": [x, y, z], "max": [x, y, z]} that is centred. Blender reports observed bounds as six numbers [xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax, zmin, zmax]; build this {min, max} object from them with {"$calc": "boundsMin"} and {"$calc": "boundsMax"}.

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/14/properties/args/.units: Blender units (scene world units; Schemaxis applies no unit conversion)

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/22.explanation: Calls fitCamera: computes a camera object (direction, up, focalPoint, bounds, parallel, scale, distance) that frames a box. In Blender documents the result has no valid destination, because camera entries accept runtime values only per field; frame with the camera's own bounds, direction and padding instead.
pitfalls: Its scale follows the ParaView half-height convention, which is too small for Blender's orthographic width.

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/22/properties/args.label: Arguments

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/22/properties/args/.explanation: Axis-aligned box as {"min": [x, y, z], "max": [x, y, z]} that the camera is fitted to. Blender reports observed bounds as six numbers [xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax, zmin, zmax]; build this {min, max} object from them with {"$calc": "boundsMin"} and {"$calc": "boundsMax"}.
/$defs/runtime/anyOf/22/properties/args/.label: Bounds
/$defs/runtime/anyOf/22/properties/args/.units: Blender units (scene world units; Schemaxis applies no unit conversion)
pitfalls: Every axis needs positive extent (min below max); a flat box fails with FUNCTION_FAILED.

/$defs/options-array/properties/count.explanation: Total number of instances in the result, including the original: 2 gives the original plus one copy. Larger counts lengthen the row and multiply the face count.
/$defs/options-array/properties/count.label: Instance count

pitfalls: A count of 1 leaves the mesh unchanged.

/$defs/options-array/properties/relative.explanation: Step between consecutive instances as [x, y, z] multiples of the input mesh's bounding-box size along its local axes (Blender relative_offset_displace). /$defs/options-array/properties/relative.units: Multiples of the input mesh's local bounding-box size (dimensionless)
pitfalls: The step is relative to the input's size, not a distance; for a fixed spacing compute it from the size or use transform on separate nodes.

/$defs/options-bend.explanation: Settings of the Simple Deform modifier in Bend mode: angle is the total bend in radians and axis the local axis it bends around. Both take Schemaxis defaults when omitted (pi/4 radians about Z); the other Simple Deform settings keep Blender's defaults.

/$defs/options-bend/properties/angle.explanation: Total bend angle in radians, spread over the mesh's extent: 1.5708 turns the ends through a right angle and 6.2832 curls the mesh into a full circle. Negative values bend the other way.

/$defs/options-bend/properties/angle.defaultMeaning: Schemaxis default: 0.7853981633974483 (pi/4, the same as Blender's new-modifier value).

/$defs/options-bevel.explanation: Settings of the Bevel modifier: width sets how far the bevel cuts back from each edge and segments how round it is. Omitted settings take Schemaxis defaults (0.1, 3 segments); unexposed Bevel settings keep Blender's defaults, including the Offset width type and the 30 degree angle limit.

/$defs/options-bevel/properties/width.explanation: Bevel size: with Blender's default Offset type it is the distance from each original edge to the new edges created on the adjacent faces. Larger values cut more material and give broader rounds; 0 leaves the edges sharp.
/$defs/options-bevel/properties/width.label: Bevel width
/$defs/options-bevel/properties/width.units: Blender units in the input object's local (mesh) coordinates
pitfalls: On a cube the local mesh spans -1..1, so width 0.1 is 5% of the edge whatever the cube size; use applyTransform first for a width in world units.

/$defs/options-bevel/properties/width/an.explanation: Bevel size: with Blender's default Offset type it is the distance from each original edge to the new edges created on the adjacent faces. Larger values cut more material and give broader rounds; 0 leaves the edges sharp.
/$defs/options-bevel/properties/width/an.units: Blender units in the input object's local (mesh) coordinates
pitfalls: On a cube the local mesh spans -1..1, so width 0.1 is 5% of the edge whatever the cube size; use applyTransform first for a width in world units.

/$defs/options-readGltf.explanation: Import settings for the glTF reader: only the source file, which is required and fixed when the node is created. Blender's glTF importer runs with its own default options.

/$defs/options-readGltf/properties/file.explanation: Path of a glTF 2.0 JSON file (.gltf) containing exactly one mesh, with buffers and images embedded as data: URIs. Relative paths are resolved against the working directory of the Schemaxis process; workflows usually pass a verified ParaView scene artifact with $artifact. The file is copied and digest-checked and is fixed when the node is created.
/$defs/options-readGltf/properties/file.label: glTF file
pitfalls: A .glb binary or a .gltf referencing external .bin or texture files is rejected (UNSUPPORTED_RESOURCE).

/$defs/options-readPLY.explanation: Import settings for the PLY reader: the required source file and a uniform scale, both fixed when the node is created. Other PLY importer options keep Blender's defaults.

/$defs/options-readPLY/properties/file.explanation: Path of the PLY file to import. Relative paths are resolved against the working directory of the Schemaxis process; in workflows an $artifact from a verified producer is usual. The file is copied into the run directory and both copies are digest-checked; it is fixed when the node is created.
/$defs/options-readPLY/properties/file.label: PLY file
pitfalls: Changing the file between run and verify fails verification with INPUT_CHANGED.
The import must yield exactly one mesh object with faces.

/$defs/options-readPLY/properties/scale.explanation: Uniform factor applied to every imported coordinate (importer global_scale; scene units ignored). PLY stores bare numbers, so this is how you set units: 0.001 makes a millimetre export metre-sized, 1 keeps the numbers.
/$defs/options-readPLY/properties/scale.label: Import scale
pitfalls: It is a constructor setting and must be a constant; sweep sizes with transform scale instead.

/$defs/runtimeValue/anyOf/1.explanation: An array argument, typically a literal or partly computed vector such as [0, 0, {"$axis": "z"}], or six-number bounds.

/$defs/runtimeValue/anyOf/1/items.explanation: One $calc argument: a literal number, string, boolean or null, an array of such values (for example a vector), or a nested runtime expression.

/$defs/runtimeValue/anyOf/2.explanation: A runtime expression: a JSON object that replaces a whole option or camera value and is evaluated for each state after upstream nodes are updated. In Blender documents it can read an axis value ($axis), the time ($time) or an updated node's observation ($observe), and combine them with $calc arithmetic or registered $call functions. The result must still satisfy the destination field. Constructor settings (reader file and scale, curveFromCSV file) cannot use it, and field sampling ($sample) is not available in Blender.

pitfalls: Material overrides, holdout, indirect-only and local viewport hiding require an explicit compositing or visibility conversion before reuse. Data-level object/collection visibility flags are retained.

Unique graph-local identity for this resource reader, used by links and native editing; not the resource alias itself.
Read a typed collection or whole-asset collection as instances, retaining nested occurrences and offsets.

Typed Object/Collection reference and instance controls. Public identities and aliases resolve to real native pointers and are checked after save/reopen. Resource cycles and conservative expansion limits refuse before modifier evaluation.
Public collection identity or collection-kind resource alias. All nested collection occurrences contribute to geometry expansion and dependency admission.
Expose the selected collection children as separate instances rather than one collection instance. Child transforms remain until resetChildren is selected.
Reset child instance transforms to the consumer origin. Requires separateChildren; this intentionally discards child placement in both ORIGINAL and RELATIVE spaces.
Choose the coordinate space used by this reviewed resource reader. The resource identity is a typed input value; this record exposes no native reflection.

ORIGINAL Object Info keeps source mesh-local numerical coordinates; RELATIVE preserves source world placement relative to the consumer, including asset scale. Collection Info includes native collection offsets. Metre-valued imported local coordinates are not automatically converted in ORIGINAL mode.

Declare finite typed aliases for an Object, selected native/glTF asset prototype, public collection or complete owned asset collection. Object aliases fill Object sockets; collection/asset aliases fill Collection sockets. No arbitrary native paths are accepted.

Unique resource alias used in typed Geometry Nodes sockets. It must differ from public Object/collection identities and other aliases; it is not an RNA expression.
Choose an Object pointer, a public Collection pointer, or the actual whole-asset owned collection. An Empty asset Object does not automatically collect ordinary child geometry.
Public Object or asset-root identity. With sourceObject, resolve one captured source prototype using pre-import name/collision proof; otherwise use the public Object itself.

Original native Object name or unique glTF mesh-node name, proven before import. Selects a prototype, not one occurrence path. Per-part modifiers affect every occurrence of that prototype. Distinct parts can have separate bindings; ambiguous/colliding identities refuse.

Original captured native Object or unique glTF mesh-node name. Selects one source prototype, including every occurrence of that prototype. Ambiguous/post-import collision names refuse; no native property expression is accepted.

refuse requires one Object owner; copy isolates the target Mesh; shared intentionally updates every Object using that Mesh. Distinct selectors resolving to the same Object refuse. Copy targets are resolved before shared targets.

/properties/scenes/items/properties/prod.explanation: Strictly positive rational NURBS weight. Larger values pull the evaluated curve toward this control; changing weight can alter interior geometry without changing bounds.
NURBS polynomial degree plus one, between two and six and no greater than the control count. Order three with rational weights can represent exact conic arcs.
Clamp an open NURBS spline to its end controls. Cyclic splines disable this setting because their knots are periodic.
Use complete quadratic/cubic Bezier-style NURBS spans. Control counts must fit the chosen order, and cyclic splines disable this setting.
2D constrains controls/handles to local XY and enables planar fill/outline offset; 3D permits spatial paths and spatial surface fill policies.
AUTO chooses BOTH for planar contours and FULL for spatial sweeps. Other choices select front/back sides or disable planar filling; incompatible dimensional choices refuse.

For planar contours, EVEN_ODD alternates inside/outside at each crossing; NONZERO fills same-winding overlap as a union. Native nonzero extrusions can retain internal walls; this is not arbitrary solid repair.
Planar sweep-line filling is fast but lacks self-intersection support. CDT supports intersections and uses a conservative quadratic intersection budget before evaluation.
Signed planar outline distance in local production units. Spatial curve offset refuses because native outline offset requires planar shape semantics.
/properties/scenes/items/properties/prod.units: Curve-local production distance units before Object/parent/asset transforms.

Sample the profile at approximately even lengths instead of following its control spacing; this changes generated section geometry, not the centreline.
Include profile straight-edge sampling when distributing section segments. The profile remains editable in the native project.
Request native end filling for swept geometry. Object profile direction affects cap/side orientation; use the qualified clockwise section direction for solid sweeps.
Sweep-frame policy along the centreline: MINIMUM minimizes twist, Z_UP anchors the frame to Z, and TANGENT follows native tangent frames.
Native frame-twist smoothing iterations between path samples. It changes the swept frame while preserving declared control positions.

Start/end factors select a subrange of swept geometry without deleting native controls. Each end has its own resolution/segment/spline mapping. Partial trimming requires constant point radius along each spline because Blender5.2 can retain an untrimmed endpoint radius.
Start factor in zero to one; it must not exceed end. This changes the swept extent and retains the editable original centreline.
End factor in zero to one; it must be at least start. Caps and taper mapping follow the resulting swept range.
Interpret the start factor by sample resolution, segment count or spline parameter, matching the corresponding native curve policy.
Interpret the end factor independently by resolution, segments or spline parameter. Different mappings can select different points on a nonuniform curve.
Optional one-open-spline planar Curve dependency whose local X maps along the path and local Y controls section radius. It requires swept geometry and participates in cycle admission.
Declared Curve Object identity or object geometry-resource alias used as a section/taper. Asset members use original native source selectors; mutable imported collision names are not authority.
OVERRIDE replaces control radii with taper values, MULTIPLY combines them multiplicatively, and ADD sums them. Nondefault taper options require a taper object.
Map taper along the trimmed sweep portion rather than the original entire spline. Useful when changing trim factors.
Retain native path/deformation controls for followPath consumers. Constraint factor authoring is currently fixed; broader animated parameter and curve-deform authoring remain required.
Enable native path evaluation for constraints and deformation consumers; retained independently from whether the Curve has swept thickness.
Native path duration in frames, used by path-time consumers. A fixed followPath factor directly selects normalized path position instead.
Enable tangent-oriented path following in Curve settings. A followPath constraint also has its own following flag and fixed normalized factor.
Apply curve radius to path followers and curve-deformed objects. This flag does not change the swept section itself.
Stretch a curve-deformed object along the path length. This retains the native deformation policy; a full curve modifier authoring family remains unfinished.
Use the deforming object bounds when mapping curve deformation along the path; this differs from a followPath constraint location factor.
