/properties/scenes/items/properties/rend.explanation: Adjust scene-linear brightness in photographic stops before the display transform. One additional stop doubles linear values.

/properties/scenes/items/properties/rend.label: Display gamma
/properties/scenes/items/properties/rend.explanation: Apply positive additional display gamma correction. Keep one for the normal view transform; this is not a texture colour-space declaration.

/properties/scenes/items/properties/rend.label: White balance
/properties/scenes/items/properties/rend.explanation: Enable illuminant temperature and tint compensation, or disable the additional white-balance transform.

/properties/scenes/items/properties/rend.label: Disabled
/properties/scenes/items/properties/rend.explanation: Enable illuminant temperature and tint compensation, or disable the additional white-balance transform. This variant chooses Disabled.

/properties/scenes/items/properties/rend.label: Disabled
/properties/scenes/items/properties/rend.explanation: Choose Disabled for this typed policy; only its declared controls are accepted.

/properties/scenes/items/properties/rend.label: Enabled
/properties/scenes/items/properties/rend.explanation: Enable illuminant temperature and tint compensation, or disable the additional white-balance transform. This variant chooses Enabled.

/properties/scenes/items/properties/rend.label: Enabled
/properties/scenes/items/properties/rend.explanation: Choose Enabled for this typed policy; only its declared controls are accepted.

/properties/scenes/items/properties/rend.label: Illuminant temperature
/properties/scenes/items/properties/rend.explanation: Specify the illuminant white-point temperature in kelvin for the enabled white-balance transform.

/properties/scenes/items/properties/rend.label: White-balance tint
/properties/scenes/items/properties/rend.explanation: Adjust the illuminant white point along Blender's tint axis. Ten is the native default; this is independent of exposure and material RGB.

/properties/scenes/items/properties/prod.label: Stored alpha
/properties/scenes/items/properties/prod.explanation: Interpret the stored alpha representation: straight keeps RGB independent with alpha as a mask; premultiplied stores RGB times alpha; channelPacked keeps all channels independent, including RGB at zero alpha; ignore makes the image opaque. This is shared by preview and shader users of the image.
pitfalls: Do not choose premultiplied for ordinary unassociated RGB, or the decoded colours change.
Native Workbench transparency is display behaviour, not a general compositing model.

/properties/scenes/items/properties/prod.label: Display image
/properties/scenes/items/properties/prod.explanation: Choose an independent Workbench image preview or the material display swatch. This does not connect the image to the shader, and applies only to root material graphs. Cycles and EEVEE evaluate the authored shader graph.
/properties/scenes/items/properties/prod.defaultMeaning: Omitting displayTexture chooses none: the material swatch.
pitfalls: Workbench needs a usable active UV map to display the image.

/properties/scenes/items/properties/prod.label: Material swatch
/properties/scenes/items/properties/prod.explanation: Explicitly use the material viewportColour for Workbench texture shading, even if other image nodes exist in its shader graph.

/properties/scenes/items/properties/prod.label: Swatch source
/properties/scenes/items/properties/prod.explanation: Explicitly use the material viewportColour for Workbench texture shading, even if other image nodes exist in its shader graph.

/properties/scenes/items/properties/prod.label: Captured image
/properties/scenes/items/properties/prod.explanation: Choose one declared captured image for Workbench preview. Its image identity and active UV map determine the display; its shader connections remain independent.

/properties/scenes/items/properties/prod.label: Image source
/properties/scenes/items/properties/prod.explanation: Choose one declared captured image for Workbench preview. Its image identity and active UV map determine the display; its shader connections remain independent.

/properties/scenes/items/properties/prod.label: Declared image
/properties/scenes/items/properties/prod.explanation: Identity of an image declared in production.images. The preview points to that captured resource, independently of Image Texture nodes used by the shader. Workbench samples the active UV map.
pitfalls: A file path or unknown image identity is refused.

/properties/scenes/items/properties/rend.label: Image texture
/properties/scenes/items/properties/rend.explanation: Display each material's selected displayTexture using the mesh's active UV map. With no selected image or usable UVs the qualified native release uses the material viewport swatch. Shader graphs and render UV selection remain independent.

/properties/scenes/items/properties/rend.label: Texture colour source
/properties/scenes/items/properties/rend.explanation: Display each material's selected displayTexture using the mesh's active UV map. With no selected image or usable UVs the qualified native release uses the material viewport swatch. Shader graphs and render UV selection remain independent.

Bake the declared rigid-body world or cloth consumers for stable saved results when frames are reopened in a different order. Declare at most 32 distinct cache IDs and consumers. Each cache covers the complete production timeline, within 1000 frames; production fps determines the time between frames. Scene ownership, runtime, constructor and source fingerprints come from trusted construction and cannot be authored here. Changed simulation inputs require fresh construction and baking; a saved cache manifest alone cannot authorize reuse.

One bake for an existing typed physics consumer in this production scene. Choose the consumer kind, logical cloth object when applicable, full timeline and storage together. Construction binds the declared physics, admitted dependencies and fixed Blender runtime. Editing geometry, physics parameters, gravity, fps, frame bounds or dependency bytes invalidates the old bake.

Unique portable cache identity: begin with a letter and use up to 63 letters, digits, underscores or hyphens. It identifies this bake and its managed payloads; it is not a native object name, file path or source-authority token.

Select the actual existing physics consumer: rigidBody bakes the scene rigid-body world; cloth bakes one declared cloth object. This does not create physics or enable other simulation families. Qualified Blender 5.2.3 supports packed rigid-body caches and packed or disk cloth caches; rigid-body disk conversion is explicitly refused because its native storage setter crashes before baking.

Logical production object ID of the declared cloth mesh consumer. For rigidBody, leave this empty: the cache belongs to the owning scene world and covers its rigid bodies. Native scene names and arbitrary native object lookup are not authored selectors.

First inclusive baked frame, equal to production.frameStart. Together with frameEnd it must cover the entire production timeline within 1000 consecutive positive frames; partial cache intervals are refused. Production fps sets physical time per frame. Changing the range or fps requires a fresh bake.

Last inclusive baked frame, equal to production.frameEnd. The complete timeline must fit within 1000 consecutive positive frames so render, export and other timeline samples cannot silently use an unbaked interval. Changing the range or production fps invalidates the old bake.

packed retains the bake inside the saved scene; disk publishes managed cloth .bphys files beside that scene in blendcache_<visit basename>/. Keep those declared files with the scene. External paths and inherited external caches are refused. Verification compares disk bytes with an independently constructed fresh bake before opening the submitted scene; packed data also requires all-frame geometry and physics checks. Rigid-body disk mode is explicitly unsupported in the qualified runtime; use packed rigid-body storage.

fields.explanation: Renders a saved Schemaxis Blender scene (a .blend published by a schemaxis.blender/1 run) from new cameras without rebuilding its geometry. It opens a retained copy of the file, replaces lighting and render settings with this document's, frames each camera on the saved visible meshes and writes one PNG per camera; verification checks that geometry and materials were unchanged by rendering.
pitfalls: Only scenes saved by Schemaxis work: the file must carry its node metadata, have no linked libraries and pack all images.

/properties/version.explanation: Identifies the document format and chooses its adaptor. Keep the version matching the selected schema.

/properties/sceneFile.explanation: The saved .blend to render, normally {"$artifact": producer, "index": n} pointing at the scene artifact of a prepareOnly Blender operation. A literal path is resolved against the working directory of the Schemaxis process; the file is copied into the run directory and its SHA-256 is checked again at verification.
/properties/sceneFile.label: Saved scene
pitfalls: The artifact index counts images and meshes before the .blend of each state; with prepareOnly and no meshes, state 0's .blend is index 0.

/properties/cameras.explanation: Literal camera views (1 to 1000), each rendered to {index}.png in list order. Runtime expressions are not available here because the saved scene is not re-evaluated.
/properties/cameras.label: Cameras

/properties/cameras/items.explanation: One camera view. Each camera produces one PNG per render job, framed on the bounds of the visible meshes recorded in the saved scene unless bounds, focalPoint, scale or distance are given. Omitted settings mean: view from +x, Z up, orthographic, automatic fit with 10% padding.

/properties/cameras/items/properties/dir.explanation: Which side of the subject the camera looks from: Blender places the camera at focalPoint + unit(direction) x distance and points it back at the focal point. "x+" or [1, 0, 0] views from +x; [1, -2, 1] gives a raised front-right view. Give an axis token, a vector, or an azimuth/elevation object.
/properties/cameras/items/properties/dir.label: View direction
pitfalls: It must not be parallel to up; for views straight down use direction "z+" with up "y+".

/properties/cameras/items/properties/dir.explanation: Axis-token spelling: names a world axis and sign, e.g. "x+", "y-" or "z+" (also "x", "+x", "xp", "xm", "-x"; case-insensitive). Choose it for directions along world axes, such as standard front, side or top views; here the token gives the side of the subject the camera is placed on: Blender puts the camera at focalPoint + direction x distance, looking back at the focal point.
pitfalls: A camera direction of "z+" or "z-" is parallel to the default up [0, 0, 1] and fails with INVALID_CAMERA; set up to "y+" for top or bottom views.

/properties/cameras/items/properties/dir.explanation: Vector spelling [x, y, z] in world axes; only its direction matters, Schemaxis normalises it. Choose it for oblique views or directions computed elsewhere; here it gives the side of the subject the camera is placed on: Blender puts the camera at focalPoint + direction x distance, looking back at the focal point.
pitfalls: [0, 0, 0] has no direction and is rejected.

/properties/cameras/items/properties/dir.explanation: One world-axis component of the direction vector: index 0 is x, 1 is y, 2 is z. Only the ratios between components matter.

Object spelling: give exactly one of axis (a token), vector, or azimuth and elevation, optionally with up as the reference axis for the angles. Choose it when a direction is easier to state as compass angles, e.g. {"azimuth": 30, "elevation": 20} for the direction 30 degrees anticlockwise from +x (seen from above) and 20 degrees above the horizontal plane. The resolved unit vector gives the side of the subject the camera is placed on: Blender puts the camera at focalPoint + direction x distance, looking back at the focal point.
pitfalls: Combining axis, vector and angles in one object fails with OVER_SPECIFIED_DIRECTION.
An omitted azimuth or elevation is taken as 0.

/properties/cameras/items/properties/dir.explanation: Axis token such as 'x+'
Degrees about the up axis from the reference axis
Degrees tilted from the plane perpendicular to up
Direction as a world-axis vector [x, y, z] inside the object form; normalised, so only its direction matters. Do not combine it with axis, azimuth or elevation.
/properties/cameras/items/properties/dir.label: Vector

/properties/cameras/items/properties/dir.explanation: One world-axis component of the object's vector: index 0 is x, 1 is y, 2 is z.

Reference axis for azimuth and elevation in this object: azimuth turns anticlockwise about it (seen from its positive side) starting from +x, or from +y when the reference is along x, and elevation tilts towards it. It is not the camera's screen-up setting.
/properties/cameras/items/properties/dir.label: Angle reference axis

/properties/cameras/items/properties/dir.explanation: Reference axis as a token such as "z+" or "y+"; choose it when angles should be measured about a world axis.
Reference axis as a vector [x, y, z], normalised; choose it when angles should be measured about a tilted axis, such as a vehicle's own vertical.
One world-axis component of the reference axis vector: index 0 is x, 1 is y, 2 is z.

/properties/cameras/items/properties/up.explanation: Which world direction appears upwards in the image. Only its part perpendicular to the view direction is used, so [0, 0, 1] keeps world Z vertical for any side view.
/properties/cameras/items/properties/up.label: Screen up
pitfalls: An up parallel to direction fails with INVALID_CAMERA.

/properties/cameras/items/properties/up/.explanation: Axis-token spelling: names a world axis and sign, e.g. "x+", "y-" or "z+" (also "x", "+x", "xp", "xm", "-x"; case-insensitive). Choose it for directions along world axes, such as standard front, side or top views; here the token gives the direction that should appear upwards in the image; Schemaxis removes its component along the viewing direction.

Vector spelling [x, y, z] in world axes; only its direction matters, Schemaxis normalises it. Choose it for oblique views or directions computed elsewhere; here it gives the direction that should appear upwards in the image; Schemaxis removes its component along the viewing direction.
pitfalls: [0, 0, 0] has no direction and is rejected.

/properties/cameras/items/properties/up/.explanation: One world-axis component of the direction vector: index 0 is x, 1 is y, 2 is z. Only the ratios between components matter.

Object spelling: give exactly one of axis (a token), vector, or azimuth and elevation, optionally with up as the reference axis for the angles. Choose it when a direction is easier to state as compass angles, e.g. {"azimuth": 30, "elevation": 20} for the direction 30 degrees anticlockwise from +x (seen from above) and 20 degrees above the horizontal plane. The resolved unit vector gives the direction that should appear upwards in the image; Schemaxis removes its component along the viewing direction.
pitfalls: Combining axis, vector and angles in one object fails with OVER_SPECIFIED_DIRECTION.
An omitted azimuth or elevation is taken as 0.

/properties/cameras/items/properties/up/.explanation: Axis token such as 'x+'
Degrees about the up axis from the reference axis
Degrees tilted from the plane perpendicular to up
Direction as a world-axis vector [x, y, z] inside the object form; normalised, so only its direction matters. Do not combine it with axis, azimuth or elevation.
/properties/cameras/items/properties/up/.label: Vector

/properties/cameras/items/properties/up/.explanation: One world-axis component of the object's vector: index 0 is x, 1 is y, 2 is z.

Reference axis for azimuth and elevation in this object: azimuth turns anticlockwise about it (seen from its positive side) starting from +x, or from +y when the reference is along x, and elevation tilts towards it. It is not the camera's screen-up setting.
/properties/cameras/items/properties/up/.label: Angle reference axis

/properties/cameras/items/properties/up/.explanation: Reference axis as a token such as "z+" or "y+"; choose it when angles should be measured about a world axis.
Reference axis as a vector [x, y, z], normalised; choose it when angles should be measured about a tilted axis, such as a vehicle's own vertical.
One world-axis component of the reference axis vector: index 0 is x, 1 is y, 2 is z.

/properties/cameras/items/properties/foc.explanation: World point [x, y, z] the camera aims at; it is the centre of the image. When set, Schemaxis skips its automatic check that the whole bounds fit inside the frame.
/properties/cameras/items/properties/foc.label: Focal point
/properties/cameras/items/properties/foc.units: Blender units (scene world units; Schemaxis applies no unit conversion)
/properties/cameras/items/properties/foc.defaultMeaning: Centre of the framing bounds (the visible meshes recorded in the saved scene, or bounds when given).
pitfalls: Moving the focal point off the bounds centre with automatic scale can crop the model; increase padding or set scale.

/properties/cameras/items/properties/foc.explanation: One world coordinate of the focal point: index 0 is x, 1 is y, 2 is z.
/properties/cameras/items/properties/foc.units: Blender units (scene world units; Schemaxis applies no unit conversion)

/properties/cameras/items/properties/par.explanation: true gives an orthographic projection (no perspective shrinking, sizes comparable across the image) sized by scale; false gives a perspective camera with the lens of a new Blender camera, which Schemaxis does not change (50 mm focal length on a 36 mm sensor).
/properties/cameras/items/properties/par.label: Orthographic
pitfalls: With false, padding and scale have no effect and Schemaxis does not check that the model fits; adjust distance to frame it.

/properties/cameras/items/properties/sca.explanation: Width of the orthographic view in world units: Blender ortho_scale with horizontal sensor fit, so the image spans scale horizontally and scale x height/width vertically. Larger values zoom out. Only used when parallel is true.
/properties/cameras/items/properties/sca.label: Orthographic width
/properties/cameras/items/properties/sca.units: Blender units (scene world units; Schemaxis applies no unit conversion)
/properties/cameras/items/properties/sca.defaultMeaning: Automatic: bounds diagonal x (1 + padding) x max(1, width/height), so the shorter image side spans the padded diagonal.
pitfalls: ParaView interprets camera scale as half the view height; the same number frames differently in Blender, and scale values returned by fitCamera or orbitCameras are too small for Blender.

/properties/cameras/items/properties/dis.explanation: Distance from the focal point to the camera along direction. For perspective views it sets how large the model appears; for orthographic views it only moves the camera, but it also sets the far clipping distance (at least distance + 2 x bounds diagonal) while the near clip is 1/10000 of the diagonal.
/properties/cameras/items/properties/dis.label: Camera distance
/properties/cameras/items/properties/dis.units: Blender units (scene world units; Schemaxis applies no unit conversion)
/properties/cameras/items/properties/dis.defaultMeaning: Automatic: twice the diagonal of the framing bounds.
pitfalls: In perspective mode, too small a distance places the camera inside the model.

/properties/cameras/items/properties/bou.explanation: Framing box [xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax, zmin, zmax] in world coordinates that replaces the bounds of the visible meshes recorded in the saved scene for this camera: its centre is the default focal point and its diagonal sets the default scale, distance and clipping. Use it to frame a region of interest or keep framing fixed across states.
/properties/cameras/items/properties/bou.label: Framing bounds
/properties/cameras/items/properties/bou.units: Blender units (scene world units; Schemaxis applies no unit conversion)
/properties/cameras/items/properties/bou.defaultMeaning: Union of the bounds of the visible meshes recorded in the saved scene.
pitfalls: The order is min/max per axis, not min corner then max corner; any min greater than its max fails with INVALID_BOUNDS.

/properties/cameras/items/properties/bou.explanation: One bound value; positions 0 to 5 are xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax, zmin, zmax.
/properties/cameras/items/properties/bou.units: Blender units (scene world units; Schemaxis applies no unit conversion)

/properties/cameras/items/properties/pad.explanation: Fractional margin for automatic orthographic framing: the shorter image side spans (1 + padding) times the bounds diagonal, so 0.1 leaves roughly 10% of extra room. Ignored when scale is set or parallel is false.
/properties/cameras/items/properties/pad.label: Padding

/properties/render.explanation: Cycles render settings, world lighting and the single area light applied when the saved scene is rendered. They replace whatever the saved scene contained: omitted keys take the Schemaxis defaults below, not the values saved in the .blend.

/properties/render/properties/device.explanation: Cycles compute backend. CPU renders anywhere and is the reproducible baseline. CUDA (NVIDIA GPUs) or OPTIX (NVIDIA RTX ray-tracing hardware) are faster for many samples; Schemaxis enables only devices of that type, reserves one GPU in workflow scheduling and fails verification unless the device use is evidenced.
/properties/render/properties/device.label: Render device
pitfalls: A GPU backend that the machine or driver lacks fails with DEVICE_UNAVAILABLE.
GPU and CPU renders of the same scene are not guaranteed to be pixel-identical.

/properties/render/properties/samples.explanation: Cycles samples per pixel (scene.cycles.samples). More samples reduce noise roughly with the square root of the count but cost proportional time; the default is a quick preview. Transmission, emission and small lights need more.
/properties/render/properties/samples.label: Samples

/properties/render/properties/threads.explanation: Fixed number of CPU threads for rendering (render threads mode FIXED). In workflows the operation's execution threads must equal this value, so the scheduler reserves exactly what Blender uses.
/properties/render/properties/threads.label: Render threads
pitfalls: A workflow execution.threads that differs fails with INVALID_EXECUTION; set both together.

/properties/render/properties/denoise.explanation: When true Cycles denoises the final image (use_denoising), giving clean images from few samples at the cost of slightly smoothed fine texture; when false the raw sampled noise remains.
/properties/render/properties/denoise.label: Denoise

/properties/render/properties/transparen.explanation: When true the world background is rendered transparent (film_transparent) for compositing over another background; the world colour still lights the model. When false the background shows worldColour.
/properties/render/properties/transparen.label: Transparent background

/properties/render/properties/seed.explanation: Cycles sampling seed. The same seed and settings reproduce the same noise pattern; changing it gives a different but statistically equivalent noise, useful to check whether a feature is noise.
/properties/render/properties/seed.label: Seed

/properties/render/properties/worldColou.explanation: Colour [red, green, blue] of the uniform world background (Background shader), 0 to 1. It is both the visible background and an ambient light from all directions, so it tints the model as well.
/properties/render/properties/worldColou.label: World colour

/properties/render/properties/worldColou.explanation: One channel of the world colour: index 0 red, 1 green, 2 blue, from 0 to 1.

/properties/render/properties/worldStren.explanation: Strength of the world background light. Higher values brighten the background and fill shadows evenly; 0 leaves only the area light (and emission), giving a black background and high contrast.
/properties/render/properties/worldStren.label: World strength

/properties/render/properties/lightEnerg.explanation: Radiant power of the single square area light that Schemaxis adds (Blender light energy). The illumination reaching the model falls with the square of the distance from lightPosition, so rescale energy when the model or the light is moved much nearer or farther.
/properties/render/properties/lightEnerg.label: Light power
pitfalls: Small parts lit from a nearby lightPosition need far less energy (the freecad-to-blender example uses 20 W at about 0.4 units).

/properties/render/properties/lightPosit.explanation: World position [x, y, z] of the area light. The light is always aimed at the world origin, not at the model, so for models far from the origin move it accordingly (or move the model to the origin).
/properties/render/properties/lightPosit.label: Light position
/properties/render/properties/lightPosit.units: Blender units (scene world units; Schemaxis applies no unit conversion)
/properties/render/properties/lightPosit.defaultMeaning: Schemaxis default: [4, -4, 6] (front-right, above, about 8.2 units from the origin).

/properties/render/properties/lightPosit.explanation: One world coordinate of the light position: index 0 is x, 1 is y, 2 is z.
/properties/render/properties/lightPosit.units: Blender units (scene world units; Schemaxis applies no unit conversion)

/properties/render/properties/lightSize.explanation: Edge length of the square area light. Larger lights give softer shadow edges; smaller ones give crisper shadows and highlights.
/properties/render/properties/lightSize.label: Light size
/properties/render/properties/lightSize.units: Blender units (scene world units; Schemaxis applies no unit conversion)

/properties/size.explanation: Output image size [width, height] in pixels, each 32 to 2048. The aspect ratio also affects the automatic orthographic width (it widens with width/height). The saved scene's own resolution is ignored.
/properties/size.label: Image size

/properties/size/items.explanation: One image dimension in pixels: index 0 is the width, index 1 the height (32 to 2048).

/properties/render/properties/renderer.label: Rendering engine
/properties/render/properties/renderer.explanation: Choose path-traced Cycles, real-time EEVEE shading or technical Workbench presentation. Each engine exposes controls that actually affect its output.

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: Cycles path tracing
/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.explanation: Choose path-traced Cycles, real-time EEVEE shading or technical Workbench presentation. Each engine exposes controls that actually affect its output. This variant chooses Cycles path tracing.

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: Cycles path tracing
/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.explanation: Choose Cycles path tracing for this typed policy; only its declared controls are accepted.

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: EEVEE real-time shading
/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.explanation: Choose path-traced Cycles, real-time EEVEE shading or technical Workbench presentation. Each engine exposes controls that actually affect its output. This variant chooses EEVEE real-time shading.

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: EEVEE real-time shading
/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.explanation: Choose EEVEE real-time shading for this typed policy; only its declared controls are accepted.

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: EEVEE render samples
/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.explanation: Set EEVEE temporal render samples. The legacy top-level samples field controls Cycles only; geometry complexity and shader compilation still affect elapsed time.

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: Ray-tracing policy
/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.explanation: Enable EEVEE screen-space tracing for supported visible geometry, or disable the tracing pipeline. Screen-space information cannot replace missing off-screen geometry or baked probes.

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: Disabled
/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.explanation: Enable EEVEE screen-space tracing for supported visible geometry, or disable the tracing pipeline. Screen-space information cannot replace missing off-screen geometry or baked probes. This variant chooses Disabled.

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: Disabled
/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.explanation: Choose Disabled for this typed policy; only its declared controls are accepted.

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: Screen-space method
/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.explanation: Enable EEVEE screen-space tracing for supported visible geometry, or disable the tracing pipeline. Screen-space information cannot replace missing off-screen geometry or baked probes. This variant chooses Screen-space method.

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: Screen-space method
/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.explanation: Choose Screen-space method for this typed policy; only its declared controls are accepted.

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: Trace resolution
/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.explanation: Choose a full, half, quarter, eighth or sixteenth render resolution for the tracing approximation. Lower resolution reduces work but loses spatial detail.

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: Ray-tracing filtering
/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.explanation: Use raw traced results or explicitly select spatial, temporal and bilateral noise reduction. A filtered policy needs at least one enabled filter.

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: No filtering
/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.explanation: Use raw traced results or explicitly select spatial, temporal and bilateral noise reduction. A filtered policy needs at least one enabled filter. This variant chooses No filtering.

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: No filtering
/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.explanation: Choose No filtering for this typed policy; only its declared controls are accepted.

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: Filtered tracing
/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.explanation: Use raw traced results or explicitly select spatial, temporal and bilateral noise reduction. A filtered policy needs at least one enabled filter. This variant chooses Filtered tracing.

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: Filtered tracing
/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.explanation: Choose Filtered tracing for this typed policy; only its declared controls are accepted.

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: Spatial reuse
/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.explanation: Reuse neighbouring pixel rays to reduce tracing noise, trading some spatial independence for smoother results.

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: Temporal reuse
/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.explanation: Accumulate traced information by reprojecting earlier samples. Moving geometry and disocclusions can limit reusable history.

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: Bilateral filtering
/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.explanation: Smooth traced radiance while retaining differences across geometric/image features. This may remove fine detail along with noise.

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: Tracing precision
/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.explanation: Control ray-marching precision for the selected approximation. Precision is independent of image size, tracing resolution and render sample count.

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: Surface thickness
/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.explanation: Approximate surface thickness in scene world units for screen-space intersection or GI occlusion. Choose it with the scene scale and thin-wall geometry in mind.

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: Backface tracing
/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.explanation: Choose single-sided tracing or allow hits on polygon backs with a controlled reuse of front-face radiance.

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: Single-sided tracing
/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.explanation: Choose single-sided tracing or allow hits on polygon backs with a controlled reuse of front-face radiance. This variant chooses Single-sided tracing.

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: Single-sided tracing
/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.explanation: Choose Single-sided tracing for this typed policy; only its declared controls are accepted.

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: Trace both sides
/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.explanation: Choose single-sided tracing or allow hits on polygon backs with a controlled reuse of front-face radiance. This variant chooses Trace both sides.

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: Trace both sides
/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.explanation: Choose Trace both sides for this typed policy; only its declared controls are accepted.

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: Backface radiance reuse
/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.explanation: Reuse this fraction of front-face illumination for the backface approximation. Zero suppresses that reuse; one uses the complete front-face illumination.

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: Fast GI approximation
/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.explanation: Approximate ambient occlusion or global illumination for surfaces above the roughness threshold. Ray tracing must be enabled; this is an approximation with resolution and sampling tradeoffs.

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: Disabled
/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.explanation: Approximate ambient occlusion or global illumination for surfaces above the roughness threshold. Ray tracing must be enabled; this is an approximation with resolution and sampling tradeoffs. This variant chooses Disabled.

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: Disabled
/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.explanation: Choose Disabled for this typed policy; only its declared controls are accepted.

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: Ambient occlusion approximation
/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.explanation: Approximate ambient occlusion or global illumination for surfaces above the roughness threshold. Ray tracing must be enabled; this is an approximation with resolution and sampling tradeoffs. This variant chooses Ambient occlusion approximation.

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: Ambient occlusion approximation
/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.explanation: Choose Ambient occlusion approximation for this typed policy; only its declared controls are accepted.

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: Trace resolution
/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.explanation: Choose a full, half, quarter, eighth or sixteenth render resolution for the tracing approximation. Lower resolution reduces work but loses spatial detail.

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: Tracing precision
/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.explanation: Control ray-marching precision for the selected approximation. Precision is independent of image size, tracing resolution and render sample count.

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: Approximation rays
/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.explanation: Set rays per fast-GI evaluation. More rays reduce directional sampling noise while increasing work.

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: Marching steps
/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.explanation: Set steps along each fast-GI ray. More steps sample intersections more finely at additional cost.

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: GI roughness threshold
/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.explanation: Use fast GI for surfaces above this roughness. One would disable the approximation and is refused when fast GI is enabled.

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: GI maximum distance
/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.explanation: Limit fast-GI ray travel in scene world units. Zero leaves the maximum unspecified; it does not mean zero-length rays.

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: Surface thickness
/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.explanation: Approximate surface thickness in scene world units for screen-space intersection or GI occlusion. Choose it with the scene scale and thin-wall geometry in mind.

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: GI self-intersection bias
/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.explanation: Offset fast-GI intersection decisions to reduce self-occlusion. Excessive bias can erase nearby contact detail.

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: Global illumination approximation
/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.explanation: Approximate ambient occlusion or global illumination for surfaces above the roughness threshold. Ray tracing must be enabled; this is an approximation with resolution and sampling tradeoffs. This variant chooses Global illumination approximation.

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: Global illumination approximation
/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.explanation: Choose Global illumination approximation for this typed policy; only its declared controls are accepted.

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.explanation: Use fast GI for surfaces above this roughness. One would disable the approximation and is refused when fast GI is enabled.

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: GI maximum distance
/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.explanation: Limit fast-GI ray travel in scene world units. Zero leaves the maximum unspecified; it does not mean zero-length rays.

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: Surface thickness
/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.explanation: Approximate surface thickness in scene world units for screen-space intersection or GI occlusion. Choose it with the scene scale and thin-wall geometry in mind.

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: GI self-intersection bias
/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.explanation: Offset fast-GI intersection decisions to reduce self-occlusion. Excessive bias can erase nearby contact detail.

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: Shadow rays
/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.explanation: Control EEVEE shadow-ray sampling. More rays can reduce shadow noise while increasing work.

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: Shadow steps
/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.explanation: Control EEVEE steps along shadow rays. More steps improve the approximation at additional render cost.

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: Workbench technical shading
/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.explanation: Choose path-traced Cycles, real-time EEVEE shading or technical Workbench presentation. Each engine exposes controls that actually affect its output. This variant chooses Workbench technical shading.

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: Workbench technical shading
/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.explanation: Choose Workbench technical shading for this typed policy; only its declared controls are accepted.

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: Technical lighting
/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.explanation: Choose Flat, a bundled Studio environment or a bundled MatCap. Workbench ignores scene lamps and shader node lighting.

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: Flat lighting
/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.explanation: Choose Flat, a bundled Studio environment or a bundled MatCap. Workbench ignores scene lamps and shader node lighting. This variant chooses Flat lighting.

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: Flat lighting
/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.explanation: Choose Flat lighting for this typed policy; only its declared controls are accepted.

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: Studio lighting
/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.explanation: Choose Flat, a bundled Studio environment or a bundled MatCap. Workbench ignores scene lamps and shader node lighting. This variant chooses Studio lighting.

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: Studio lighting
/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.explanation: Choose Studio lighting for this typed policy; only its declared controls are accepted.

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: Bundled lighting preset
/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.explanation: Choose a named Studio environment or MatCap bundled with the supported Blender runtime. User replacements and custom preset paths are not silently substituted.

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: World-space Studio lighting
/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.explanation: Keep Studio lighting fixed in world space instead of following the view. This enables an explicit environment rotation.

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: Studio environment rotation
/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.explanation: Rotate world-space Studio lighting around its Z axis in radians. A nonzero rotation requires worldSpace true.

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: Studio specular highlights
/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.explanation: Include Studio-light specular highlights in technical shading. This option belongs to Studio presets with a specular pass, not the bundled MatCaps.

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: MatCap lighting
/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.explanation: Choose Flat, a bundled Studio environment or a bundled MatCap. Workbench ignores scene lamps and shader node lighting. This variant chooses MatCap lighting.

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: MatCap lighting
/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.explanation: Choose MatCap lighting for this typed policy; only its declared controls are accepted.

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: Bundled lighting preset
/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.explanation: Choose a named Studio environment or MatCap bundled with the supported Blender runtime. User replacements and custom preset paths are not silently substituted.

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: Technical colour source
/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.explanation: Choose material swatches, geometric Object colours, mesh colour attributes, native object-based random colours or one uniform RGB colour. These sources have distinct authored meanings.

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: Material display colours
/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.explanation: Choose material swatches, geometric Object colours, mesh colour attributes, native object-based random colours or one uniform RGB colour. These sources have distinct authored meanings. This variant chooses Material display colours.

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: Object display colours

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: Object-based random colours

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: Mesh colour attributes

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.explanation: Choose Mesh colour attributes for this typed policy; only its declared controls are accepted.

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: One display colour
/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.explanation: Choose material swatches, geometric Object colours, mesh colour attributes, native object-based random colours or one uniform RGB colour. These sources have distinct authored meanings. This variant chooses One display colour.

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: One display colour

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: Display RGB colour

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: Background colour

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: RGB component
/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.explanation: One scene-linear red, green or blue component. The display view and exposure determine its encoded PNG value; it is independent of shader lighting.

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: Edge antialiasing
/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.explanation: Choose Workbench edge smoothing or disable it for direct pixel checks. More temporal samples reduce jagged edges at additional render cost.

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: Technical shadows
/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.explanation: Enable Workbench shadows with a declared direction and darkness, or disable them. This does not use scene lamp transforms or energy.

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: Disabled
/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.explanation: Enable Workbench shadows with a declared direction and darkness, or disable them. This does not use scene lamp transforms or energy. This variant chooses Disabled.

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: Disabled
/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.explanation: Choose Disabled for this typed policy; only its declared controls are accepted.

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: Enabled
/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.explanation: Enable Workbench shadows with a declared direction and darkness, or disable them. This does not use scene lamp transforms or energy. This variant chooses Enabled.

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: Enabled

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: Shadow direction
/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.explanation: Specify a nonzero Workbench light direction. The planner normalizes it without changing its direction; this is independent of scene lamps.

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: Direction component
/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.explanation: One X, Y or Z component of the nonzero shadow direction; the planner normalizes the complete direction vector.

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: Shadow darkness
/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.explanation: Set the Workbench shadow intensity. Zero removes darkening; one uses full shadow intensity.

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: Shadow position shift
/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.explanation: Adjust the Workbench shadow offset to control shadow placement and surface self-shadowing.

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: Shadow focus
/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.explanation: Adjust the Workbench shadow focus, controlling the transition between lit and shadowed surfaces.

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: Cavity emphasis
/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.explanation: Emphasize concave and convex surface features in world space, screen space or both. This is technical illustration shading, not a geometry modification.

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: Disabled
/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.explanation: Emphasize concave and convex surface features in world space, screen space or both. This is technical illustration shading, not a geometry modification. This variant chooses Disabled.

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: World-space cavity

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: World-space cavity
/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.explanation: Choose World-space cavity for this typed policy; only its declared controls are accepted.

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: Ridge strength
/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.explanation: Increase emphasis on convex surface features in the selected cavity method. Screen-space and world-space strengths have different ranges.

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: Valley strength
/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.explanation: Increase emphasis on concave surface features in the selected cavity method. This changes shading, not mesh depth.

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: Screen-space method
/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.explanation: Emphasize concave and convex surface features in world space, screen space or both. This is technical illustration shading, not a geometry modification. This variant chooses Screen-space method.

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: Screen-space method

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: Ridge strength

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: Valley strength
/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.explanation: Increase emphasis on concave surface features in the selected cavity method. This changes shading, not mesh depth.

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: World and screen cavity
/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.explanation: Emphasize concave and convex surface features in world space, screen space or both. This is technical illustration shading, not a geometry modification. This variant chooses World and screen cavity.

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: World and screen cavity
/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.explanation: Choose World and screen cavity for this typed policy; only its declared controls are accepted.

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: World-space ridge strength
/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.explanation: Emphasize convex features using world-space cavity shading when both cavity methods are enabled.

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: World-space valley strength
/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.explanation: Emphasize concave features using world-space cavity shading when both cavity methods are enabled.

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: Screen-space ridge strength
/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.explanation: Emphasize convex features from screen-space curvature when both cavity methods are enabled.

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: Screen-space valley strength
/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.explanation: Emphasize concave features from screen-space curvature when both cavity methods are enabled.

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: Object outline
/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.explanation: Draw an explicit object outline colour or disable outlines. This is distinct from Freestyle and Grease Pencil line art.

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: Disabled
/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.explanation: Draw an explicit object outline colour or disable outlines. This is distinct from Freestyle and Grease Pencil line art. This variant chooses Disabled.

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: Disabled
/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.explanation: Choose Disabled for this typed policy; only its declared controls are accepted.

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: Enabled
/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.explanation: Draw an explicit object outline colour or disable outlines. This is distinct from Freestyle and Grease Pencil line art. This variant chooses Enabled.

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: Disabled

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: Xray opacity
/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.explanation: Set Workbench xray surface opacity between zero and one. This is independent of PNG film transparency and shader alpha.

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: Cull back-facing surfaces
/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.explanation: Hide back-facing polygons in Workbench. Use consistent winding for open shells; this does not close a mesh or repair normals.

/properties/render/properties/colourMana.label: Display transform
/properties/render/properties/colourMana.explanation: Control how scene-linear shading becomes the displayed PNG, independently of the rendering engine and texture input colour spaces.

/properties/render/properties/colourMana.label: Display view
/properties/render/properties/colourMana.explanation: Choose an explicit bundled view transform. Standard/sRGB supports direct colour-patch expectations; AgX, Neutral and ACES tone mapping change highlight appearance.

/properties/render/properties/colourMana.label: AgX tone mapping
/properties/render/properties/colourMana.explanation: Choose an explicit bundled view transform. Standard/sRGB supports direct colour-patch expectations; AgX, Neutral and ACES tone mapping change highlight appearance. This variant chooses AgX tone mapping.

/properties/render/properties/colourMana.explanation: Choose AgX tone mapping for this typed policy; only its declared controls are accepted.

/properties/render/properties/colourMana.label: Raw view
/properties/render/properties/colourMana.explanation: Choose Raw view for this typed policy; only its declared controls are accepted.

/properties/render/properties/colourMana.label: Exposure
/properties/render/properties/colourMana.explanation: Adjust scene-linear brightness in photographic stops before the display transform. One additional stop doubles linear values.

/properties/render/properties/colourMana.label: Display gamma
/properties/render/properties/colourMana.explanation: Apply positive additional display gamma correction. Keep one for the normal view transform; this is not a texture colour-space declaration.

/properties/render/properties/colourMana.label: White balance
/properties/render/properties/colourMana.explanation: Enable illuminant temperature and tint compensation, or disable the additional white-balance transform.

/properties/render/properties/colourMana.explanation: Choose Enabled for this typed policy; only its declared controls are accepted.

/properties/render/properties/colourMana.label: Illuminant temperature
/properties/render/properties/colourMana.explanation: Specify the illuminant white-point temperature in kelvin for the enabled white-balance transform.

/properties/render/properties/colourMana.label: White-balance tint
/properties/render/properties/colourMana.explanation: Adjust the illuminant white point along Blender's tint axis. Ten is the native default; this is independent of exposure and material RGB.

/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.label: Image texture
/properties/render/properties/renderer/a.explanation: Display each material's selected displayTexture using the mesh's active UV map. With no selected image or usable UVs the qualified native release uses the material viewport swatch. Shader graphs and render UV selection remain independent.

Cycles built-in shader execution backend. Omission or svm selects historical SVM. osl enables built-in Open Shading Language nodes on CPU or OptiX and is required for Smart image filtering; no Script node or authored shader code is enabled. The configured runtime must include OSL.

fields.explanation: Compose complete scene production from named assets, motion, appearance and reusable presentation intent, without authoring a mesh DAG. The same native executor preserves original authored input and verifies the deterministic lowered scene.

/properties/version.explanation: Scene-production document contract version, separate from the Blender application release. This route accepts complete typed scene records without authored graph scaffolding.

/properties/id.explanation: Stable scene identity retained in the lowered execution and publications.

/properties/production.explanation: Compose named scene assets, hierarchy, motion, rigs, node graphs and frame publications around the mesh graph. The saved project stays editable; the strategic family map lists remaining workflows.

/properties/production/properties/frameS.explanation: First integer frame of the production timeline and sequential simulation evaluation. Use the same origin for imported motion and requested publications.

/properties/production/properties/frameE.explanation: Last integer frame of the production timeline. Keys, renders, exports and simulation samples must lie within the inclusive start/end range.

/properties/production/properties/fps.explanation: Timeline frames per second. Together with frame numbers this sets motion duration and physical simulation elapsed time; it does not resample authored keyframes.

/properties/production/properties/curren.explanation: Frame retained in the saved project and used for exports that omit their frame. If omitted it is frameStart; output jobs restore this frame after evaluation.
/properties/production/properties/curren.defaultMeaning: Omitting currentFrame uses frameStart, which is1by default.

/properties/production/properties/gravit.explanation: World acceleration vector for native physics. The default points down world Z at9.81metres per second squared; Blender applies the scene physical unit scale.

World acceleration vector for native physics. The default points down world Z at9.81metres per second squared; Blender applies the scene physical unit scale. This record describes one ordered entry/component of that field.

/properties/production/properties/units.explanation: Physical length represented by one numerical scene coordinate. The blend retains these numbers and its scene scale. GLB/USD export in metres; OBJ/PLY/STL retain the declared numerical units with explicit metadata. Choose among metres, millimetres, centimetres, inches, feet.

/properties/production/properties/collec.explanation: Named reusable scene collections, optionally nested. Declare contents through object collection references, and reuse the complete contents through collectionInstance assets.
/properties/production/properties/collec.defaultMeaning: Omit this optional collection when no entries of this kind are needed; required variant collections are identified by the schema.

/properties/production/properties/collec.explanation: Named reusable scene collections, optionally nested. Declare contents through object collection references, and reuse the complete contents through collectionInstance assets. This record describes one ordered entry/component of that field.
Stable authored identity within this record family. Use names in references instead of native list positions; duplicate identities in the same namespace are refused.
Named parent in the same hierarchy. Collection and bone parents must exist; object parenting may reference mesh-graph outputs or production objects. Cyclic relationships are refused.

/properties/production/properties/hierar.explanation: Object parenting relationships. Each object has at most one parent; keepWorld decides whether parenting preserves its original world pose or its authored local pose.
/properties/production/properties/hierar.defaultMeaning: Omit this optional collection when no entries of this kind are needed; required variant collections are identified by the schema.

/properties/production/properties/hierar.explanation: Object parenting relationships. Each object has at most one parent; keepWorld decides whether parenting preserves its original world pose or its authored local pose. This record describes one ordered entry/component of that field.
Named target object. Mesh graph outputs and declared production assets share the object reference space; materials cannot be substituted for geometry.
Named parent in the same hierarchy. Collection and bone parents must exist; object parenting may reference mesh-graph outputs or production objects. Cyclic relationships are refused.
Preserve the initial world pose when assigning the parent. False retains the local transform so the parent contributes immediately to the world pose.

/properties/production/properties/materi.explanation: Replace the target geometric object material with a named graph material or mesh-graph material. Shared object data also shares material slots.
/properties/production/properties/materi.defaultMeaning: Omit this optional collection when no entries of this kind are needed; required variant collections are identified by the schema.

/properties/production/properties/materi.explanation: Replace the target geometric object material with a named graph material or mesh-graph material. Shared object data also shares material slots. This record describes one ordered entry/component of that field.
Named target object. Mesh graph outputs and declared production assets share the object reference space; materials cannot be substituted for geometry.
Named material resource to assign. It must refer to a mesh-graph material or production material graph; mesh exchange formats can lose this appearance.

/properties/production/properties/geomet.explanation: Attach a named Geometry Nodes graph to a geometric object as an editable modifier. Procedural topology expansion is bounded before native evaluation.
/properties/production/properties/geomet.defaultMeaning: Omit this optional collection when no entries of this kind are needed; required variant collections are identified by the schema.

/properties/production/properties/geomet.explanation: Attach a named Geometry Nodes graph to a geometric object as an editable modifier. Procedural topology expansion is bounded before native evaluation. This record describes one ordered entry/component of that field.
Named target object. Mesh graph outputs and declared production assets share the object reference space; materials cannot be substituted for geometry.
Named geometry graph to attach to this object. Graph references are checked before launching Blender; shader and compositor graphs have different roles.

/properties/production/properties/images.explanation: File-backed image assets for material graphs. Original and retained bytes are hashed; packing embeds the image in the saved project rather than relying on an external path.
/properties/production/properties/images.defaultMeaning: Omit this optional collection when no entries of this kind are needed; required variant collections are identified by the schema.

/properties/production/properties/images.explanation: File-backed image assets for material graphs. Original and retained bytes are hashed; packing embeds the image in the saved project rather than relying on an external path. This record describes one ordered entry/component of that field.
Stable authored identity within this record family. Use names in references instead of native list positions; duplicate identities in the same namespace are refused.

Input image path. Original and retained bytes must stay identical during capture and verification. Files are bounded to 64 MiB each / 256 MiB aggregate; decoded images to 4,194,304 pixels each / 16,777,216 aggregate and 8192 per axis. PNG/JPEG dimensions are checked before native decode; other formats immediately after load. Use its declared image identity in shader nodes and displayTexture.
How Blender interprets image samples. sRGB decodes colour textures; Non-Color preserves numeric data such as normals or masks. Choose among sRGB, Non-Color.
Embed image bytes into the saved project. False retains an external dependency whose bytes are still captured and verified; portable projects normally use true.

/properties/production/properties/rigs.explanation: Editable armatures with named rest bones. Bone heads/tails define the rest frame, hierarchy defines joint chains and skin bindings define deformation weights.

/properties/production/properties/rigs/i.explanation: Editable armatures with named rest bones. Bone heads/tails define the rest frame, hierarchy defines joint chains and skin bindings define deformation weights. This record describes one ordered entry/component of that field.

/properties/production/properties/render.explanation: Unique integer frames to render as additional PNGs. The saved current frame and active camera are restored afterward; these publications are separate from the legacy static camera images.
/properties/production/properties/render.defaultMeaning: Omit this optional collection when no entries of this kind are needed; required variant collections are identified by the schema.

/properties/production/properties/render.explanation: Unique integer frames to render as additional PNGs. The saved current frame and active camera are restored afterward; these publications are separate from the legacy static camera images. This record describes one ordered entry/component of that field.

/properties/production/properties/camera.explanation: Named camera for production frame rendering. Omit to use the existing automatically framed camera; a mesh/light cannot be substituted.

/properties/visible.explanation: Named geometric assets or scene roots used for framing and geometry observations. Omit to select declared assets and geometric production objects; root selection includes evaluated descendants. Individual production hidden flags still govern rendering.

/properties/visible/items.explanation: Named geometric assets or scene roots used for framing and geometry observations. Omit to select declared assets and geometric production objects; root selection includes evaluated descendants. Individual production hidden flags still govern rendering.

/properties/render.explanation: Cycles render settings, world lighting and the single area light used for every image of this scene and stored in the saved .blend. Omitted keys take the Schemaxis defaults shown on each field; samples, denoise and the light most affect image quality.

/properties/render/properties/device.explanation: Cycles compute backend. CPU renders anywhere and is the reproducible baseline. CUDA (NVIDIA GPUs) or OPTIX (NVIDIA RTX ray-tracing hardware) are faster for many samples; Schemaxis enables only devices of that type, reserves one GPU in workflow scheduling and fails verification unless the device use is evidenced.
/properties/render/properties/device.label: Render device
pitfalls: A GPU backend that the machine or driver lacks fails with DEVICE_UNAVAILABLE.
GPU and CPU renders of the same scene are not guaranteed to be pixel-identical.

/properties/render/properties/samples.explanation: Cycles samples per pixel (scene.cycles.samples). More samples reduce noise roughly with the square root of the count but cost proportional time; the default is a quick preview. Transmission, emission and small lights need more.
/properties/render/properties/samples.label: Samples

/properties/render/properties/threads.explanation: Fixed number of CPU threads for rendering (render threads mode FIXED). In workflows the operation's execution threads must equal this value, so the scheduler reserves exactly what Blender uses.
/properties/render/properties/threads.label: Render threads
pitfalls: A workflow execution.threads that differs fails with INVALID_EXECUTION; set both together.

/properties/render/properties/denoise.explanation: When true Cycles denoises the final image (use_denoising), giving clean images from few samples at the cost of slightly smoothed fine texture; when false the raw sampled noise remains.
/properties/render/properties/denoise.label: Denoise

/properties/render/properties/transparen.explanation: When true the world background is rendered transparent (film_transparent) for compositing over another background; the world colour still lights the model. When false the background shows worldColour.
/properties/render/properties/transparen.label: Transparent background

/properties/render/properties/seed.explanation: Cycles sampling seed. The same seed and settings reproduce the same noise pattern; changing it gives a different but statistically equivalent noise, useful to check whether a feature is noise.
/properties/render/properties/seed.label: Seed

/properties/render/properties/worldColou.explanation: Colour [red, green, blue] of the uniform world background (Background shader), 0 to 1. It is both the visible background and an ambient light from all directions, so it tints the model as well.
/properties/render/properties/worldColou.label: World colour

/properties/render/properties/worldColou.explanation: One channel of the world colour: index 0 red, 1 green, 2 blue, from 0 to 1.

/properties/render/properties/worldStren.explanation: Strength of the world background light. Higher values brighten the background and fill shadows evenly; 0 leaves only the area light (and emission), giving a black background and high contrast.
/properties/render/properties/worldStren.label: World strength

/properties/render/properties/lightEnerg.explanation: Radiant power of the single square area light that Schemaxis adds (Blender light energy). The illumination reaching the model falls with the square of the distance from lightPosition, so rescale energy when the model or the light is moved much nearer or farther.
/properties/render/properties/lightEnerg.label: Light power
pitfalls: Small parts lit from a nearby lightPosition need far less energy (the freecad-to-blender example uses 20 W at about 0.4 units).

/properties/render/properties/lightPosit.explanation: World position [x, y, z] of the area light. The light is always aimed at the world origin, not at the model, so for models far from the origin move it accordingly (or move the model to the origin).
/properties/render/properties/lightPosit.label: Light position
/properties/render/properties/lightPosit.units: Blender units (scene world units; Schemaxis applies no unit conversion)
/properties/render/properties/lightPosit.defaultMeaning: Schemaxis default: [4, -4, 6] (front-right, above, about 8.2 units from the origin).

/properties/render/properties/lightPosit.explanation: One world coordinate of the light position: index 0 is x, 1 is y, 2 is z.
/properties/render/properties/lightPosit.units: Blender units (scene world units; Schemaxis applies no unit conversion)

/properties/render/properties/lightSize.explanation: Edge length of the square area light. Larger lights give softer shadow edges; smaller ones give crisper shadows and highlights.
/properties/render/properties/lightSize.label: Light size
/properties/render/properties/lightSize.units: Blender units (scene world units; Schemaxis applies no unit conversion)

/properties/prepareOnly.explanation: Save an editable project without the legacy static preview image. Explicit renderFrames and exports still publish their requested outputs.

/properties/size.explanation: PNG output dimensions [width,height] in pixels for both the preview and requested frame renders. The default is320by240; each side is32–2048.

/properties/size/items.explanation: PNG output dimensions [width,height] in pixels for both the preview and requested frame renders. The default is320by240; each side is32–2048.

/properties/cameras.explanation: Camera views rendered for every state, in list order. It may also be an $analytic orbit sequence, which expands into one camera per azimuth.
/properties/cameras.label: Cameras

/properties/cameras/items.explanation: One camera view. Each camera produces one PNG per state (unless prepareOnly), framed on the bounds of the scene's visible meshes in the current state unless bounds, focalPoint, scale or distance are given. Omitted settings mean: view from +x, Z up, orthographic, automatic fit with 10% padding. Values may be runtime expressions, for example bounds from $observe.

/properties/cameras/items/properties/dir.explanation: Which side of the subject the camera looks from: Blender places the camera at focalPoint + unit(direction) x distance and points it back at the focal point. "x+" or [1, 0, 0] views from +x; [1, -2, 1] gives a raised front-right view. Give an axis token, a vector, or an azimuth/elevation object.
/properties/cameras/items/properties/dir.label: View direction
pitfalls: It must not be parallel to up; for views straight down use direction "z+" with up "y+".

/properties/cameras/items/properties/dir.explanation: Which side of the subject the camera looks from: Blender places the camera at focalPoint + unit(direction) x distance and points it back at the focal point. "x+" or [1, 0, 0] views from +x; [1, -2, 1] gives a raised front-right view. Give an axis token, a vector, or an azimuth/elevation object.

In Blender documents it can read an axis value ($axis), the time ($time) or an updated node's observation ($observe), and combine them with $calc arithmetic or registered $call functions. The result must still satisfy the destination field. Constructor settings (reader file and scale, curveFromCSV file) cannot use it, and field sampling ($sample) is not available in Blender.
One world-axis component of the direction vector: index 0 is x, 1 is y, 2 is z. Only the ratios between components matter.

/properties/cameras/items/properties/up/.explanation: Reference axis for azimuth and elevation in this object: azimuth turns anticlockwise about it (seen from its positive side) starting from +x, or from +y when the reference is along x, and elevation tilts towards it. It is not the camera's screen-up setting.
/properties/cameras/items/properties/up/.label: Angle reference axis

/properties/cameras/items/properties/up/.explanation: One world-axis component of the reference axis vector: index 0 is x, 1 is y, 2 is z.

/properties/cameras/items/properties/foc.explanation: World point [x, y, z] the camera aims at; it is the centre of the image. When set, Schemaxis skips its automatic check that the whole bounds fit inside the frame.
/properties/cameras/items/properties/foc.label: Focal point
/properties/cameras/items/properties/foc.units: Blender units (scene world units; Schemaxis applies no unit conversion)
/properties/cameras/items/properties/foc.defaultMeaning: Centre of the framing bounds (the scene's visible meshes in the current state, or bounds when given).
pitfalls: Moving the focal point off the bounds centre with automatic scale can crop the model; increase padding or set scale.

/properties/cameras/items/properties/foc.explanation: One world coordinate of the focal point: index 0 is x, 1 is y, 2 is z.
/properties/cameras/items/properties/foc.units: Blender units (scene world units; Schemaxis applies no unit conversion)

/properties/cameras/items/properties/par.explanation: true gives an orthographic projection (no perspective shrinking, sizes comparable across the image) sized by scale; false gives a perspective camera with the lens of a new Blender camera, which Schemaxis does not change (50 mm focal length on a 36 mm sensor).
/properties/cameras/items/properties/par.label: Orthographic
pitfalls: With false, padding and scale have no effect and Schemaxis does not check that the model fits; adjust distance to frame it.

/properties/cameras/items/properties/sca.explanation: Width of the orthographic view in world units: Blender ortho_scale with horizontal sensor fit, so the image spans scale horizontally and scale x height/width vertically. Larger values zoom out. Only used when parallel is true.
/properties/cameras/items/properties/sca.label: Orthographic width
/properties/cameras/items/properties/sca.units: Blender units (scene world units; Schemaxis applies no unit conversion)
/properties/cameras/items/properties/sca.defaultMeaning: Automatic: bounds diagonal x (1 + padding) x max(1, width/height), so the shorter image side spans the padded diagonal.
pitfalls: ParaView interprets camera scale as half the view height; the same number frames differently in Blender, and scale values returned by fitCamera or orbitCameras are too small for Blender.

/properties/cameras/items/properties/dis.explanation: Distance from the focal point to the camera along direction. For perspective views it sets how large the model appears; for orthographic views it only moves the camera, but it also sets the far clipping distance (at least distance + 2 x bounds diagonal) while the near clip is 1/10000 of the diagonal.
/properties/cameras/items/properties/dis.label: Camera distance
/properties/cameras/items/properties/dis.units: Blender units (scene world units; Schemaxis applies no unit conversion)
/properties/cameras/items/properties/dis.defaultMeaning: Automatic: twice the diagonal of the framing bounds.
pitfalls: In perspective mode, too small a distance places the camera inside the model.

/properties/cameras/items/properties/bou.explanation: Framing box [xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax, zmin, zmax] in world coordinates that replaces the bounds of the scene's visible meshes in the current state for this camera: its centre is the default focal point and its diagonal sets the default scale, distance and clipping. Use it to frame a region of interest or keep framing fixed across states.
/properties/cameras/items/properties/bou.label: Framing bounds
/properties/cameras/items/properties/bou.units: Blender units (scene world units; Schemaxis applies no unit conversion)
/properties/cameras/items/properties/bou.defaultMeaning: Union of the bounds of the scene's visible meshes in the current state.
pitfalls: The order is min/max per axis, not min corner then max corner; any min greater than its max fails with INVALID_BOUNDS.

/properties/cameras/items/properties/bou.explanation: One bound value; positions 0 to 5 are xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax, zmin, zmax.
/properties/cameras/items/properties/bou.units: Blender units (scene world units; Schemaxis applies no unit conversion)

/properties/cameras/items/properties/pad.explanation: Fractional margin for automatic orthographic framing: the shorter image side spans (1 + padding) times the bounds diagonal, so 0.1 leaves roughly 10% of extra room. Ignored when scale is set or parallel is false.
/properties/cameras/items/properties/pad.label: Padding

/properties/maxPublications.explanation: Positive publication budget covering the native project, static previews, requested frame PNGs and every selected geometry export. Exceeding it refuses before native execution.
